title.zh: 卷四百十一 列傳第一百七十 湯璹 蔣重珍 牟子才 朱貔孫 歐陽守道
title.en: Volume 411 Biographies 170: Tang Shu, Jiang Zhongzhen, Mou Zicai, Zhu Pisun, Ouyang Shoudao
title.raw: 卷四百十一 列傳第一百七十 湯璹 蔣重珍 牟子才 朱貔孫 歐陽守道 Volume 411 Biographies 170: Tang Shu, Jiang Zhongzhen, Mou Zicai, Zhu Pisun, Ouyang Shoudao

sentences.zh: 楊棟姚希得包恢常挺陳宗禮常家鉉翁李庭芝

translations.literal: Yang Dong, Yao Xide, Bao Hui, Chang Ting, Chen Zongli, Chang Mao, Jia Xuanweng, and Li Tingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dong, Yao Xide, Bao Hui, Chang Ting, Chen Zongli, Chang Mao, Jia Xuanweng, and Li Tingzhi.

sentences.zh: 楊棟，字元極，眉州青城人。

translations.literal: Yang Dong, styled Yuanji, was a native of Qingcheng in Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dong, whose style name was Yuanji, came from Qingcheng in Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 紹定二年進士第二。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoding he placed second in the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1229 he finished second in the jinshi civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 授簽書劍南西川節度判官廳公事。

translations.literal: He was appointed as a signing clerk in the office of the military commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He received an appointment as signing clerk in the Jiannan West Circuit commissioner’s office.

sentences.zh: 未上，丁母憂。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post, he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, his mother died and he went into mourning.

sentences.zh: 服除，遷荊南製置司，改辟西川，入為太學正。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he moved to the Jingnan Pacification Commission, was then recruited into West Sichuan, and entered the capital as director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period he served on the Jingnan Pacification Commission, was later recruited in western Sichuan, and then entered the capital as director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服除，召試授秘書省正字兼吳益王府教授，遷校書郎、樞密院編修官。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his father; when mourning ended he was summoned for examination and appointed collator in the Secretariat, concurrently professor in the Prince of Wu-Yi’s household, then promoted to proofreader and compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After his father’s death and the end of mourning, he was examined and appointed collator in the Secretariat while also teaching in the household of Prince Wu-Yi; he was later promoted to proofreader and compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 入對，言：“飛蝗蔽天，願陛下始終一德，庶幾感格天心，消弭災咎。

translations.literal: He was received in audience and said: “Locusts blot out the sky; I hope Your Majesty will maintain a single consistent virtue, so that perhaps Heaven’s heart may be moved and calamities dispelled.”
translations.idiomatic: At an imperial audience he said, “Locusts are blotting out the sky. I beg Your Majesty to hold fast to one consistent virtue, so that Heaven may be moved and these disasters may pass.”

sentences.zh: ”又言：“邇來中外之臣，如主兵理財，聽其言無非可用，跡其實類皆欺誣，上下相蒙，無一可信。

translations.literal: ” He also said: “Of late, ministers within and without the court who manage troops or finances—hear their words and none seem unusable; trace their deeds and all alike prove deceit. High and low deceive one another; none can be trusted.”
translations.idiomatic: He went on, “Lately the ministers who run the armies and the treasury sound wholly capable when they speak, yet their actions are almost all deceit. Court and provinces deceive one another, and nothing they say can be trusted.”

sentences.zh: 陛下先之以至誠，而後天下之事可為也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty leads with utmost sincerity, then the affairs of the realm may afterward be undertaken.”
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty leads with utmost sincerity, then the affairs of the realm can be set right.”

sentences.zh: ”又言：“祖宗立國，不恃兵財法，惟恃民心固結而已。

translations.literal: ” He also said: “When our ancestors founded the state, they did not rely on armies, wealth, or laws alone, but only on binding the people’s hearts firmly together.”
translations.idiomatic: He also said, “Our founders did not rely on armies, treasure, or statutes alone—they relied on keeping the people’s hearts bound to the throne.”

sentences.zh: 願陛下常存忠厚之意，勿用峻急之人。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will constantly preserve a spirit of generous loyalty and not employ harsh and precipitate men.”
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to keep a spirit of generous loyalty and not to employ harsh, precipitate men.”

sentences.zh: ”理宗悅，以臣僚言奉祠。

translations.literal: ” Emperor Lizong was pleased, but on the remonstrance of other officials he was given a temple sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, but other officials objected and he was given a temple sinecure instead.

sentences.zh: 起知興化軍。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Xinghua Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed prefect of Xinghua Circuit.

sentences.zh: 孔子之裔有居氵亟頭鎮者，棟為建廟辟田，訓其子弟。

translations.literal: Descendants of Confucius lived at Jietou Town; Dong built a temple for them, opened fields, and instructed their sons and younger kin.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius’s descendants lived at Jietou Town; Dong built them a temple, set aside land, and taught their sons and younger kin.

sentences.zh: 遷福建提點刑獄，尋加直秘閣兼權知福州，兼本路安撫使，遷都官郎官，又遷左司郎官，尋為右司郎官兼玉牒所檢討官，除宗正少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Fujian judicial intendant, soon added as a member of the Privy Archives and acting prefect of Fuzhou, concurrently pacification commissioner of that circuit; he was promoted to an officer in the Ministry of Justice, then to the Left Department, soon made an officer of the Right Department and compiler at the Imperial Genealogy Office, and appointed vice director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He became Fujian judicial intendant, was soon made a Privy Archives scholar and acting prefect of Fuzhou with concurrent charge of the circuit’s pacification, rose through the Justice and Left and Right Department posts, served as compiler at the Imperial Genealogy Office, and was appointed vice director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 進對，帝曰：“止是正心修身之說乎？

translations.literal: At an audience the emperor said: “Is it only the doctrine of rectifying the mind and cultivating the person?”
translations.idiomatic: At an audience the emperor asked, “Is that all—just the teaching about rectifying the mind and cultivating the person?”

sentences.zh: ”棟對曰：“臣所學三十年，止此一說。

translations.literal: ” Dong replied: “What this subject has studied for thirty years is only this one doctrine.”
translations.idiomatic: Dong answered, “For thirty years what I have studied has been only this one teaching.”

sentences.zh: 用之事親取友，用之治凋郡、察冤獄，至為簡易。

translations.literal: Apply it to serving parents and choosing friends; apply it to governing depleted prefectures and examining wrongful cases—it is in the end quite simple.”
translations.idiomatic: Apply it in serving parents and choosing friends, in governing depleted prefectures and examining wrongful cases—it is, in the end, quite simple.”

sentences.zh: ”時有女冠出入宮禁，頗通請謁，外廷多有以為言者。

translations.literal: ” At the time a Daoist nun went in and out of the palace precincts and was much involved in requests and audiences; many at the outer court spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a Daoist nun was entering and leaving the palace and was widely used for petitions and audiences, and many at court spoke against it.

sentences.zh: 棟上疏曰：“陛下何惜一女冠，天下所側目而不亟去之乎？

translations.literal: Dong submitted a memorial saying: “Why should Your Majesty spare one Daoist nun whom the realm watches askance and not remove her at once?”
translations.idiomatic: Dong memorialized the throne: “Why should Your Majesty spare one Daoist nun whom the whole realm watches with dismay, and not remove her at once?”

sentences.zh: ”帝不謂然。

translations.literal: ” The emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor disagreed.

sentences.zh: 棟曰：“此人密交小人，甚可慮也。

translations.literal: Dong said: “This person secretly associates with petty men; she is greatly to be feared.”
translations.idiomatic: Dong said, “She secretly consorts with petty men—that is deeply worrying.”

sentences.zh: ”又言：“ 京、襄、兩淮、四川殘破郡縣之吏，多是兵將權攝，科取無藝，其民可矜，非陛下哀之，誰實哀之。

translations.literal: ” He also said: “In the ruined prefectures and counties of the capital region, Xiangyang, the two Huai circuits, and Sichuan, the officials are mostly generals and officers holding power provisionally; they levy exactions without limit. Their people deserve pity—if Your Majesty does not pity them, who truly will?”
translations.idiomatic: He also said, “In the ravaged prefectures of the capital region, Xiangyang, the two Huai, and Sichuan, officials are mostly generals holding provisional authority who levy exactions without restraint. Those people deserve pity—if Your Majesty does not pity them, who will?”

sentences.zh: ”帝從之。

translations.literal: ” The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 遷太常少卿、起居郎，差知滁州，以殿中侍御史周坦論罷。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of rites and recorder of the emperor’s words, assigned to know Chuzhou, and dismissed on the remonstrance of the palace censor Zhou Tan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of rites and recorder of the emperor’s words, assigned as prefect of Chuzhou, and dismissed after Palace Censor Zhou Tan impeached him.

sentences.zh: 起直龍圖閣、知建寧府，不拜。

translations.literal: He was recalled as a member of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Jianning Prefecture, but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as a Dragon Diagram Hall scholar and prefect of Jianning, but declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 提舉千秋鴻禧觀，遷起居郎兼權侍左侍郎、崇政殿說書，繼遷吏部侍郎兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰兼侍讀，以集英殿修撰兼中書舍人兼侍講，出知太平州，以右補闕蕭泰來論罷，依舊職提舉太平興國宮。

translations.literal: He was made superintendent of the Qianqiu Hongxi Abbey, promoted to recorder of the emperor’s words with concurrent acting left vice minister and lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, then to vice minister of personnel with concurrent co-compiler of the national history and veritable records and reader-in-waiting; as a compiler of the Jiying Hall with concurrent drafting secretary and lecturer he went out as prefect of Taiping, was dismissed on the remonstrance of the remonstrance official Xiao Tailai, and in his former capacity was made superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He superintended the Qianqiu Hongxi Abbey, became recorder of the emperor’s words with concurrent acting left vice minister and lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, then vice minister of personnel with concurrent duties on the national history and as reader-in-waiting; as Jiying Hall compiler and drafting secretary he went out as prefect of Taiping, was dismissed after Remonstrance Official Xiao Tailai objected, and was made superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Abbey in his former rank.

sentences.zh: 起知婺州。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 召奏事，以舊職奉祠。

translations.literal: He was summoned to report on affairs, then given a temple sinecure in his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to report on affairs, then given a temple sinecure at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 度宗立為太子，帝親擢棟太子詹事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Duzong was established as heir apparent, the emperor personally selected Dong as grand tutor of the heir.
translations.idiomatic: When Duzong was made heir apparent, the emperor personally appointed Dong grand tutor of the heir.

sentences.zh: 遷工部侍郎，仍為詹事兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰兼中書舍人，兼直學士院，權刑部尚書兼國子祭酒，遷禮部尚書，加端明殿學士、同簽書樞密院事兼太子賓客，進同知樞密院事兼權參知政事，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of works while remaining grand tutor, with concurrent co-compiler of the national history and veritable records and drafting secretary, member of the Hanlin Academy, acting minister of justice and director of the Imperial University, then minister of rites; he was made a scholar of the Duanming Hall, co-signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs and guest of the heir, advanced to associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs with acting vice grand councilor, and appointed vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of works while remaining grand tutor with concurrent duties on the national history, as drafting secretary and Hanlin academician, then acting minister of justice and director of the Imperial University, then minister of rites; he became a Duanming Hall scholar, co-signatory at the Bureau of Military Affairs and guest of the heir, then associate director of the bureau with acting vice grand councilor, and finally vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 台州守王華甫建上蔡書院，言於朝，乞棟為山主，詔從之。

translations.literal: Wang Huafu, prefect of Taizhou, built the Shangcai Academy and petitioned the court to appoint Dong as its head; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huafu, prefect of Taizhou, founded the Shangcai Academy and asked the court to make Dong its head; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 因卜居於台。

translations.literal: He therefore chose a residence in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He accordingly made his home in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋授資政殿學士、知建寧府，不拜。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the title of scholar of the Zizheng Hall and prefect of Jianning, but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made a Zizheng Hall scholar and prefect of Jianning, but again declined.

sentences.zh: 以舊職提舉洞霄宮，復依舊職知慶元府、沿海製置使。

translations.literal: In his former rank he was made superintendent of the Dongxiao Abbey, then again in his former rank was made prefect of Qingyuan and coastal pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At his former rank he superintended the Dongxiao Abbey, then was again appointed prefect of Qingyuan and coastal pacification commissioner at the same rank.

sentences.zh: 以監察御史胡用虎言罷，仍奉祠。

translations.literal: He was dismissed on the remonstrance of the investigating censor Hu Yonghu and again given a temple sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Hu Yonghu impeached him and he was dismissed, again receiving a temple sinecure.

sentences.zh: 加觀文殿學士知慶元府、沿海製置使，又不拜，仍奉祠。

translations.literal: He was made a scholar of the Guanwen Hall, prefect of Qingyuan, and coastal pacification commissioner, again did not accept, and again received a temple sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Guanwen Hall scholar with concurrent posts as prefect of Qingyuan and coastal pacification commissioner, declined once more, and again held a temple sinecure.

sentences.zh: 乃以資政殿大學士充萬壽觀使。

translations.literal: He was then made grand academician of the Zizheng Hall and superintendent of the Wanshou Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed grand academician of the Zizheng Hall and superintendent of the Wanshou Abbey.

sentences.zh: 卒，遺表上，帝輟朝，特贈少保。

translations.literal: He died; his final memorial was presented; the emperor suspended court and specially posthumously enfeoffed him as Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his final memorial reached the throne; the emperor suspended court and posthumously enfeoffed him as Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 棟之學本諸周、程氏，負海內重望。

translations.literal: Dong’s learning was rooted in the Zhou and Cheng schools and he bore great renown throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Dong’s learning came from the Zhou and Cheng traditions, and he enjoyed great renown throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 方賈似道入相，登用故老，列之從官，棟亦預焉。

translations.literal: When Jia Sidao entered the chancellorship he raised up old worthies and placed them among attendant officials; Dong was also included.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Sidao became chief councilor he brought back elder statesmen and placed them among his attendants; Dong was among them.

sentences.zh: 及彗星見，棟乃言蚩尤旗，非彗也，故為世所少雲。

translations.literal: When a comet appeared, Dong said it was the Banner of Chiyou, not a comet, and for this was little praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet appeared, Dong insisted it was the Banner of Chiyou rather than a comet, and for this won little praise.

sentences.zh: 或謂棟姑為是言，陰告於帝，謀逐似道，似道覺之，遂蒙疑而去。

translations.literal: Some said Dong made this remark only for show, secretly informing the emperor and plotting to drive out Sidao; Sidao became aware of it, and Dong accordingly fell under suspicion and left office.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Dong spoke thus only for appearance’s sake while secretly urging the emperor to oust Sidao; Sidao found out, Dong fell under suspicion, and he left office.

sentences.zh: 所著有《崇道集》、《平舟文集》。

translations.literal: His writings include the Chongdao Collection and the Pingzhou Anthology.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Chongdao Collection and the Pingzhou Anthology.

sentences.zh: 姚希得，字逢原，一字叔剛，潼川人，嘉定十六年進士。

translations.literal: Yao Xide, styled Fengyuan and also Shugang, was a native of Tongchuan and a jinshi of the sixteenth year of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xide, whose style names were Fengyuan and Shugang, came from Tongchuan and passed the jinshi examination in 1223.

sentences.zh: 授小溪主簿，待次三年，朝夕討論《六經》、諸子百家之言。

translations.literal: He was appointed registrar of Xiaoxi; during three years awaiting assignment he discussed morning and evening the Six Classics and the writings of the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed registrar of Xiaoxi, he spent three years awaiting assignment studying the Six Classics and the hundred schools from morning till night.

sentences.zh: 調盤石令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be magistrate of Panshi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Panshi.

sentences.zh: 會蜀有兵難，軍需調度不擾而集，更調嘉定府司理參軍。

translations.literal: When Sichuan had military troubles, he gathered military supplies without disturbing the people and was transferred to be judicial aide in Jiading Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out in Sichuan he mustered military supplies without harassing the people and was transferred to judicial aide in Jiading Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 改知蒲江縣。

translations.literal: He was changed to serve as magistrate of Pujiang County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Pujiang County.

sentences.zh: 巨室挾勢，邑號難治。

translations.literal: Great clans wielded power; the county was called hard to govern.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful local clans dominated the county, which was known as difficult to govern.

sentences.zh: 希得綏強扶弱，聲聞著聞。

translations.literal: Xide pacified the strong and supported the weak; his reputation became widely known.
translations.idiomatic: Xide restrained the powerful and aided the weak, and his reputation spread widely.

sentences.zh: 同知樞密院事遊似以希得名聞，召審察，遷行在都進奏院，通判太平州，改福州，徒步至候官，吏不知為通判也。

translations.literal: You Si, associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, heard of Xide’s fame and had him summoned for review; he was moved to the capital memorial office, made vice prefect of Taiping, then of Fuzhou; he walked on foot to Houguan, and the clerks did not know he was the vice prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Associate Director You Si of the Bureau of Military Affairs heard of Xide’s reputation and had him summoned for review; he served at the capital memorial office, as vice prefect of Taiping, then of Fuzhou, walking on foot to Houguan so that the clerks did not even recognize him as vice prefect.

sentences.zh: 召為國子監丞，遷太府寺丞，時暫書擬金部文字兼沂靖王府教授。

translations.literal: He was summoned as vice director of the Directorate of Education, promoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, and for a time drafted documents for the Ministry of Revenue and concurrently taught in the Prince of Yi-Jing’s household.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as vice director of the Directorate of Education, promoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, temporarily drafted Revenue Ministry documents, and concurrently taught in the household of Prince Yi-Jing.

sentences.zh: 時帝斥逐權奸，收召名德，舉朝相慶。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor expelled powerful traitors and recalled men of renown; the whole court rejoiced together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had just expelled powerful traitors and recalled men of renown, and the whole court rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 希得以為外觀形狀，似若清明之朝；

translations.literal: Xide considered that outward appearance made it seem like a clear and enlightened court;
translations.idiomatic: Xide thought that outward appearances made the court seem clear and enlightened;

sentences.zh: 內察脈息，有類危亡之證。

translations.literal: but inwardly examining the pulse, there were signs resembling those of imminent ruin.
translations.idiomatic: but when he felt the pulse within, he found signs like those of a state nearing collapse.

sentences.zh: 乃上疏言：“堯、舜、三代之時，無危亡之事，而常喜危亡之言；

translations.literal: He therefore submitted a memorial saying: “In the age of Yao and Shun and the Three Dynasties there were no events of ruin, yet they always welcomed words of ruin;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: “Under Yao, Shun, and the Three Dynasties there was no ruin, yet rulers welcomed talk of ruin;

sentences.zh: 秦、漢以來，多危亡之事，而常諱危亡之言。

translations.literal: since Qin and Han there have been many events of ruin, yet they constantly taboo words of ruin.
translations.idiomatic: since Qin and Han there have been many ruinations, yet rulers constantly taboo such talk.”

sentences.zh: 夫危亡之事不可有，而危亡之言不可亡。

translations.literal: Events of ruin must not exist, yet words of ruin must not perish.
translations.idiomatic: Ruin itself must not come about, but talk of ruin must never die out.”

sentences.zh: 後世人主乃履危如履坦，諱言如諱病。

translations.literal: Later sovereigns tread danger as if on level ground and taboo words as they taboo illness.”
translations.idiomatic: Later rulers tread on danger as if it were level ground and shun such words as they shun sickness.”

sentences.zh: ”又言：“君子非不收召，而意向猶未調一；

translations.literal: ” He also said: “Worthies are not unreceived, yet their intentions are still not harmonized as one;
translations.idiomatic: He also said, “Worthies are being recalled, yet their intentions are not yet unified;

sentences.zh: 小人非不斥逐，而根株猶未痛斷。

translations.literal: petty men are not undismissed, yet their roots and stems are still not cut off in pain.
translations.idiomatic: petty men are being expelled, yet their roots are not yet cut out entirely.

sentences.zh: 大權若操握，而不能無旁蹊曲逕之疑；

translations.literal: Great power seems grasped, yet one cannot be free of suspicion of side paths and winding tracks;
translations.idiomatic: Great power seems held firmly, yet suspicion of back channels remains;

sentences.zh: 大勢若更張，而未見有長治久安之道。

translations.literal: the great trend seems renewed, yet no way of long order and lasting peace is seen.
translations.idiomatic: the great reform seems under way, yet no path to lasting peace is in sight.

sentences.zh: 廷臣之所諷諫，封囊之所奏陳，非不激切，而陛下固不之罪，亦不之行。

translations.literal: The admonitions of court ministers and the memorials in sealed pouches are not unstrenuous, yet Your Majesty neither punishes them nor carries them out.
translations.idiomatic: Court remonstrances and sealed memorials are earnest enough, yet Your Majesty neither punishes them nor acts on them.”

sentences.zh: 自古甘蹈危亡之機，非獨暗主，而明君亦有焉，此臣之所甚懼。

translations.literal: From antiquity those willing to tread the brink of ruin were not only benighted rulers; enlightened rulers have also done so—this is what this subject greatly fears.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout history rulers willing to court ruin were not only benighted ones—enlightened rulers have done so too. That is what I fear most.”

sentences.zh: 朝廷者，萬化之所自出也，實根於人君之一心。

translations.literal: The court is where the myriad transformations issue forth; it is truly rooted in the sovereign’s single mind.
translations.idiomatic: The court is where all transformations begin; it is truly rooted in the sovereign’s mind alone.”

sentences.zh: 夫何大明當天，猶有可議者？

translations.literal: How is it that with great brightness dominating the heavens, there are still matters open to dispute?
translations.idiomatic: How can there still be matters in dispute when great brightness fills the heavens?”

sentences.zh: 內小學之建，人皆知陛下有意建儲也。

translations.literal: The establishment of the inner elementary school—everyone knows Your Majesty intends to establish an heir.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knows that establishing the inner elementary school shows Your Majesty intends to name an heir.”

sentences.zh: 然歲月逾邁，未睹施行，人心危疑，無所係屬。

translations.literal: Yet as the months and years pass, implementation is not seen; people’s hearts are anxious and doubtful, with nothing to which to attach.
translations.idiomatic: Yet months and years pass without action; hearts grow anxious and doubtful, with nothing to hold to.”

sentences.zh: 秦、漢而下，嗣不蚤定，事出倉卒，或宮闈出令，或宦寺主謀，或奸臣首議，此皆足以危人之國也。

translations.literal: From Qin and Han downward, when the succession was not settled early, affairs arose in haste—sometimes orders issued from the inner palace, sometimes eunuchs took the lead in plotting, sometimes treacherous ministers initiated counsel; all these were enough to endanger a state.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qin and Han, when succession was not settled early, crises arose in haste—orders from the inner palace, plots led by eunuchs, or schemes begun by treacherous ministers—all enough to endanger a state.”

sentences.zh: 陛下何憚而不蚤定大計？

translations.literal: Why should Your Majesty hesitate and not settle the great plan early?
translations.idiomatic: Why should Your Majesty hesitate to settle this great matter early?”

sentences.zh: 邸第之盛，人皆知篤於親愛也。

translations.literal: The grandeur of princely mansions—everyone knows Your Majesty is devoted to kinship love.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knows the splendor of the princely mansions shows Your Majesty’s deep affection for kin.”

sentences.zh: 然依馮者眾，輕視王法，請托之行，捷於影響。

translations.literal: Yet those who rely on such patronage are many; they slight royal law, and the practice of requests and entreaties is swifter than shadow following form.
translations.idiomatic: Yet many lean on such patronage, scorn the law, and petitions move faster than shadow follows form.”

sentences.zh: 楊幹，晉侯弟也，亂行於曲梁，而魏絳戮其仆，晉侯始怒而終悔，晉卒以霸。

translations.literal: Yang Gan was the younger brother of the Marquis of Jin; he committed disorderly conduct at Quiliang, yet Wei Jiang executed his servants; the marquis was at first angry but finally repented, and Jin in the end became hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gan, younger brother of the Marquis of Jin, misconducted himself at Quiliang; Wei Jiang executed his attendants; the marquis was angry at first but later repented, and Jin eventually became hegemon.”

sentences.zh: 平原君，趙王弟也，不出租稅，而趙奢刑其用事者，趙王賢而用之，趙卒以強。

translations.literal: Lord Pingyuan was the younger brother of the King of Zhao; he did not pay rent and tax, yet Zhao She punished those who acted for him; the king deemed him worthy and employed him, and Zhao in the end grew strong.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Pingyuan, the King of Zhao’s brother, paid no rent or tax; Zhao She punished his agents; the king valued him and employed him, and Zhao grew strong.”

sentences.zh: 皆足以興人之國也。

translations.literal: Both were enough to raise up a state.
translations.idiomatic: Both examples show how a state can be revived.”

sentences.zh: 陛下何為而不少伸國法？

translations.literal: Why does Your Majesty not extend state law even a little?
translations.idiomatic: Why does Your Majesty not enforce the law even a little among kin?”

sentences.zh: 今女冠者流，眾所指目；

translations.literal: Now the class of Daoist nuns is what the multitude points at;
translations.idiomatic: Today Daoist nuns are what everyone points at;

sentences.zh: 近璫小臣，時竊威福。

translations.literal: nearby eunuch petty officials at times steal authority and blessing.
translations.idiomatic: nearby eunuchs and petty officials at times steal power and favor.”

sentences.zh: 此皆陛下之心乍明乍晦之所致，豈不謂之危乎？

translations.literal: All these come from Your Majesty’s mind now bright, now dim—is this not called danger?
translations.idiomatic: All this comes from Your Majesty’s mind turning bright and dim by turns—is that not danger?”

sentences.zh: 國有善類，猶人有元氣，善類一敗一消，元氣一病一衰。

translations.literal: A state has good types as a person has primordial qi; when good types fail one by one they vanish, and when primordial qi sickens it declines.
translations.idiomatic: A state has good men as a person has vital energy; as good men fail and fade, so vital energy sickens and wanes.”

sentences.zh: 善類能幾，豈堪數消，消極則國隨之矣。

translations.literal: Good types are but few—how can they bear repeated extinction? When extinction reaches its limit the state follows it.
translations.idiomatic: Good men are few—how can they bear repeated losses? When they are gone, the state follows.”

sentences.zh: 陛下明於知人，公於用人，固無權奸再用之意。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is clear in knowing men and fair in employing them; you certainly have no intention of reusing powerful traitors.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty knows men clearly and employs them fairly and surely has no wish to reuse powerful traitors.”

sentences.zh: 然道路之人往往竊議，此元祐、紹聖將分之機也。

translations.literal: Yet people on the roads often whisper in private—this is the moment when Yuanyou and Shaosheng were about to divide.
translations.idiomatic: Yet people on the roads whisper—this is like the moment before the Yuanyou and Shaosheng factions split.”

sentences.zh: 禍根猶伏而未去，不幾於安其危乎？

translations.literal: The roots of calamity still lie hidden and are not removed—is this not nearly treating danger as safety?
translations.idiomatic: The roots of disaster still lie hidden—is that not treating danger as safety?”

sentences.zh: ”帝改容曰：“朕決不用史嵩之。”

translations.literal: ” The emperor changed expression and said: “I will certainly not employ Shi Songzhi.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor’s expression changed. “I will never employ Shi Songzhi,” he said.”

sentences.zh: 遷知大宗正丞兼權金部郎官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director of the Imperial Clan Court with acting officer in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Imperial Clan Court with acting duties in the Revenue Ministry.

sentences.zh: 李韶以病告，十上疏欲去。

translations.literal: Li Shao reported illness and submitted ten memorials wishing to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shao reported illness and submitted ten memorials asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 希得言：“韶有德望，雖以病告，曷若留奉內祠，侍經幄，亦足為朝廷重。

translations.literal: Xide said: “Shao has virtue and standing; though he reports illness, how much better to retain him in an inner abbey sinecure, attending the classics mat—he would still be weight for the court.”
translations.idiomatic: Xide said, “Shao has virtue and standing; though ill, better to keep him at an inner abbey sinecure attending the classics mat—he would still lend weight to the court.”

sentences.zh: ”又言：“ 財用困竭，民生憔悴，移此不急之費，以實軍儲，以厚民生，敬天莫大於此，豈在崇大宮宇，莊嚴設像哉！

translations.literal: ” He also said: “Revenue is exhausted and the people’s livelihood is worn; shift these non-urgent expenditures to fill military stores and enrich the people’s livelihood—nothing honors Heaven more than this. Is it in enlarging palaces and halls and solemnly setting up images?”
translations.idiomatic: He also said, “Treasury and people are exhausted; shift non-urgent spending to fill military stores and relieve the people—nothing honors Heaven more. Is reverence found in enlarging palaces and setting up images?”

sentences.zh: ”又條救錢楮三策，請置惠民局，帝皆以為可行。

translations.literal: ” He also set forth three policies to rescue paper money, requesting the establishment of a Bureau to Benefit the People; the emperor deemed all feasible.
translations.idiomatic: He also laid out three policies to rescue paper currency and asked for a Bureau to Benefit the People; the emperor approved all of them.”

sentences.zh: 進秘書丞，尋遷著作郎，授江西提舉常平。

translations.literal: He was advanced to secretary of the Secretariat, soon promoted to compiler, and appointed Jiangxi intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Secretariat secretary, then compiler, and appointed Jiangxi intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries.

sentences.zh: 役法久壞，臨川富室有賂吏求免者，希得竟罪之。

translations.literal: The labor-service law had long been broken; wealthy households in Linchuan bribed clerks seeking exemption, and Xide in the end punished them.
translations.idiomatic: The labor-service law had long broken down; wealthy families in Linchuan bribed clerks to escape service, and Xide punished them.

sentences.zh: 遂提點刑獄，加直秘閣。

translations.literal: He was then made judicial intendant and added as a member of the Privy Archives.
translations.idiomatic: He then became judicial intendant and was made a Privy Archives scholar.

sentences.zh: 未幾，加度支員外郎，尋直寶章閣，移治贛州。

translations.literal: Before long he was made an outer aide in the Ministry of Revenue, soon a member of the Baozhang Pavilion, and transferred to govern Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made an outer aide in the Revenue Ministry, then a Baozhang Pavilion scholar, and transferred to govern Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 盜有偽號“崔太尉”者，據石壁，連結數郡；

translations.literal: A bandit who took the false title “Grand Marshal Cui” held Shibi and linked several prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: A bandit calling himself Grand Marshal Cui held Shibi and linked several prefectures;

sentences.zh: 劉老龍等聚眾焚掠，一方繹騷。

translations.literal: Liu Laolong and others gathered crowds to burn and plunder, and the region was in continuous alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laolong and others gathered mobs to burn and plunder, throwing the region into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 希得指授方略，不五旬平之。

translations.literal: Xide directed strategy, and within less than fifty days they were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Xide directed operations and pacified them in less than fifty days.

sentences.zh: 以直寶謨閣、廣西轉運判官兼權靜江府。

translations.literal: He was made direct associate of the Baomoge Pavilion, Guangxi transport commissioner-assistant, and acting prefect of Jingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed direct associate of the Baomoge Pavilion, Guangxi transport commissioner-assistant, with acting authority over Jingjiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尋授直徽猷閣、知靜江府、主管廣西經略安撫司公事兼轉運判官。

translations.literal: Soon he was granted direct associate of the Huiyu Pavilion, prefect of Jingjiang, and charge of Guangxi pacification commissionerate affairs, concurrently transport commissioner-assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made direct associate of the Huiyu Pavilion, prefect of Jingjiang, in charge of the Guangxi pacification commissionerate while retaining his transport post.

sentences.zh: 母喪，免。

translations.literal: His mother died; he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he left office for mourning.

sentences.zh: 召為秘書少監兼中書門下省檢正諸房公事。

translations.literal: He was summoned as vice director of the Secretariat, concurrently rectifier of the various bureaus of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice director of the Secretariat with concurrent duty rectifying the various bureaus of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 入對，言君子小人邪正之辯，且曰：“君子犯顏敢諫，拂陛下之意，退甘家食，此乃為國計，非為身計也。

translations.literal: He attended audience and spoke on the distinction between gentleman and petty man, right and wrong, saying: “The gentleman offends the countenance and dares remonstrate, goes against Your Majesty’s intent, and in retirement is content with family sustenance—this is planning for the state, not for the person.”
translations.idiomatic: At audience he spoke on the difference between gentlemen and petty men, right and wrong, and said, “A gentleman offends you to your face and dares remonstrate, goes against your wishes, and in retirement is content with a private life—that is planning for the state, not for himself.”

sentences.zh: 小人自植朋黨，擠排正人，甘言佞語，一切順陛下之意，遂取陛下官爵，此乃為身計，非為國計也。

translations.literal: “The petty man on his own plants factions, squeezes out upright men, uses sweet words and flattery, wholly follows Your Majesty’s intent, and thereby takes Your Majesty’s offices and ranks—this is planning for the person, not for the state.”
translations.idiomatic: “The petty man builds factions, drives out upright men, flatters you in everything you wish, and so wins your offices and ranks—that is planning for himself, not for the state.”

sentences.zh: ”遷宗正少卿兼國史編修、實錄檢討兼權給事中，兼權刑部侍郎、同修國史、實錄院同修撰。

translations.literal: ” He was moved to vice director of the Imperial Clan Court, concurrently compiler of the National History, examiner of the Veritable Records, acting supervising secretary, acting vice minister of Justice, and co-compiler of the National History and Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Imperial Clan Court, compiler of the National History, examiner of the Veritable Records, acting supervising secretary and acting vice minister of Justice, and co-compiler at the National History and Veritable Records offices.

sentences.zh: 時西方用兵，有為嵩之復出計者，謂非此人不能辦。

translations.literal: At the time the west was at war; some plotted Songzhi’s return, saying without this man it could not be managed.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was fighting in the west, and some plotted to bring Shi Songzhi back, claiming no one else could manage it.

sentences.zh: 帝有意再用，知希得必執之，出旨諭意，希得毅然具疏密奏，不報。

translations.literal: The emperor intended to employ him again; knowing Xide would certainly hold fast, he issued an edict stating his intent; Xide resolutely submitted a full confidential memorial, with no response.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to reuse him; knowing Xide would oppose it, he issued an edict stating his intent. Xide resolutely submitted a confidential memorial in full, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 又繳鄧泳予祠之命。

translations.literal: He also returned the order granting Deng Yong a temple sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: He also returned the order granting Deng Yong a temple sinecure.

sentences.zh: 右正言邵澤、監察御史吳衍、殿中侍御史朱熠相繼論罷。

translations.literal: Right remonstrator Shao Ze, investigating censor Wu Yan, and palace censor Zhu Yi were in succession impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Right remonstrator Shao Ze, investigating censor Wu Yan, and palace censor Zhu Yi were impeached and dismissed one after another.

sentences.zh: 久之，以集英殿修撰提點千秋鴻禧觀。

translations.literal: After a long while he was made Hanlin academy compiler and intendant of the Qianqiu Hongxi Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was made Hanlin academy compiler and intendant of the Qianqiu Hongxi Abbey.

sentences.zh: 未幾，依舊職兩淮宣撫使司判官，俄加寶謨閣待制，移京西、湖南北、四川。

translations.literal: Before long he resumed his former post as commissioner-assistant of the Huai-East and Huai-West pacification office; soon he was added as Baomoge Pavilion academician and transferred through Jingxi, Hunan North and South, and Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned as commissioner-assistant of the Two Huai pacification office, was made Baomoge Pavilion academician, and served in Jingxi, Hunan North and South, and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 詔敘復元官。

translations.literal: An edict ordered restoration of his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored his original rank.

sentences.zh: 護江陵有功，召為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: For merit in defending Jiangling he was summoned as vice minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: For defending Jiangling he was summoned as vice minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“姚希得才望可為閫帥。

translations.literal: The emperor said: “Yao Xide’s talent and standing can serve as a frontier commander.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, “Yao Xide’s talent and standing suit him for frontier command.”

sentences.zh: ”乃進煥章閣待制、知慶元府、沿海製置使，繼升敷文閣待制。

translations.literal: ” He was then advanced to Huanzhang Pavilion academician, prefect of Qingyuan, and coastal commissioner; he was next promoted to Fuwen Pavilion academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Huanzhang Pavilion academician, prefect of Qingyuan, and coastal commissioner, then promoted to Fuwen Pavilion academician.

sentences.zh: 詔增沿海舟師，希得為之廣募水軍，造戰艦，蓄糧食，蠲米一萬二千石、舊逋一百萬。

translations.literal: An edict increased coastal naval forces; Xide for this widely recruited river troops, built warships, stored grain, and remitted twelve thousand piculs of rice and one million in old arrears.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict enlarged the coastal fleet, Xide widely recruited sailors, built warships, stored grain, and remitted twelve thousand piculs of rice and a million in old arrears.

sentences.zh: 去官，庫餘羨悉以代民輸。

translations.literal: On leaving office, the treasury surplus he wholly used to pay the people’s levies in their stead.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving office he used the entire treasury surplus to pay levies owed by the people.

sentences.zh: 召為工部尚書兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was summoned as minister of Works, concurrently reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as minister of Works and reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 入侍經筵，帝問慶元之政甚悉。

translations.literal: He entered to serve at the classics mat; the emperor questioned him on Qingyuan administration very thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: At the classics mat the emperor questioned him thoroughly on affairs in Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 以華文閣直學士、沿江製置使知建康府、江東安撫使、行宮留守。

translations.literal: He was made Huawen Pavilion academician, Yangtze coastal commissioner, prefect of Jiankang, Jiangdong pacification commissioner, and palace resident.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Huawen Pavilion academician, Yangtze coastal commissioner, prefect of Jiankang, Jiangdong pacification commissioner, and palace resident.

sentences.zh: 希得按行江上，慰勞士卒，眾皆歡說。

translations.literal: Xide inspected along the river, comforted and rewarded the troops, and all rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Xide toured the river line, comforted the troops, and the men rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 溧陽饑，發稟勸分，全活者眾。

translations.literal: Liyang suffered famine; he issued granary grain and urged sharing; many were wholly kept alive.
translations.idiomatic: When Liyang suffered famine he opened granaries and urged sharing, saving many lives.

sentences.zh: 創寧江軍，自建康、太平至池州列砦置屋二萬餘間，屯戍七千餘人。

translations.literal: He created the Ningjiang Army: from Jiankang and Taiping to Chizhou he set up stockades in a line, erected more than twenty thousand rooms, and garrisoned more than seven thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He created the Ningjiang Army, building more than twenty thousand quarters in stockades from Jiankang and Taiping to Chizhou and stationing over seven thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，一再降詔獎諭。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and repeatedly issued edicts of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of it and repeatedly issued edicts praising him.

sentences.zh: 加寶章閣學士，尋加刑部尚書，依舊任兼淮西總領。

translations.literal: He was added as Baozhang Pavilion academician; soon he was added as minister of Justice, retaining his former posts while concurrently Huai-West chief steward.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Baozhang Pavilion academician, soon minister of Justice as well, retaining his posts while also serving as Huai-West chief steward.

sentences.zh: 景定五年，召為兵部尚書兼侍讀。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jingding he was summoned as minister of War, concurrently reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingding year 5 he was summoned as minister of War and reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 乃言用人才、修政事、治兵甲、惜財用四事。

translations.literal: He then spoke on four matters: employing talent, repairing government, ordering arms and armor, and sparing expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke on four matters: employing talent, repairing government, ordering arms, and sparing expenditure.

sentences.zh: 拜端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事兼太子賓客。

translations.literal: He was appointed Duanming Hall academician, deputy signer of the Bureau of Military Affairs, concurrently guest of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Duanming Hall academician, deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and guest of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 公星變，上疏引咎，乞解機務。

translations.literal: A public star changed; he submitted a memorial taking blame and begging to be released from state secrets.
translations.idiomatic: When a public star changed he memorialized taking blame and asked to leave state affairs.

sentences.zh: 兼權參知政事。

translations.literal: He was concurrently acting participant in governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 度宗即位，授同知樞密院事兼權參知政事，尋授參知政事。

translations.literal: When Duzong took the throne he was granted associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, concurrently acting participant in governance; soon he was granted participant in governance.
translations.idiomatic: When Duzong succeeded he was made associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and acting vice grand councilor, then full vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 以言罷，授資政殿學士、提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: He was dismissed on account of his words and granted Zizheng Hall academician and intendant of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed after remonstrance, he was made Zizheng Hall academician and intendant of the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 起知潭州、湖南安撫使，以疾甚，辭，乃仍舊職奉祠。

translations.literal: He was raised to prefect of Tanzhou and Hunan pacification commissioner; because his illness was severe he declined, and so resumed his former post in temple service.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as prefect of Tanzhou and Hunan pacification commissioner, he declined because of grave illness and returned to his temple sinecure.

sentences.zh: 請致仕，詔不許，力請，以資政殿大學士、金紫光祿大夫、依舊潼川郡公致仕。

translations.literal: He requested retirement; the edict did not permit it; he pressed the request forcefully and retired as grand academician of the Zizheng Hall, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, retaining his former title as Duke of Tongchuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire; the court refused, but he pressed again and retired as grand academician of the Zizheng Hall, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, still Duke of Tongchuan.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianchun he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xianchun year 5.

sentences.zh: 遺表聞，帝輟朝，贈少保。

translations.literal: When his death memorial was heard, the emperor halted court and posthumously granted him Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When his final memorial arrived the emperor halted court and posthumously made him Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 希得忠亮平實，清儉自將，好引善類，不要虛譽，蓋有誦薦於上而其人莫之知者。

translations.literal: Xide was loyal, bright, level, and solid, frugal in self-conduct, fond of advancing good types, and unwilling to seek empty reputation; there were those recommended above in praise whom the man himself did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Xide was loyal, upright, plain, and frugal, fond of advancing good men and scorning empty fame; he would recommend people to the throne who never knew he had spoken for them.

sentences.zh: 廣西官署以錦為帟幕，希得曰：“吾起身書生安用此！

translations.literal: The Guangxi government office used brocade for curtains and screens; Xide said: “I rose from a mere scholar—what use have I for this!”
translations.idiomatic: The Guangxi government used brocade for curtains; Xide said, “I am only a scholar risen from the ranks—what need have I for this!”

sentences.zh: ”命以繒纈易之。

translations.literal: ” He ordered it exchanged for plain silk.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered it replaced with plain silk.

sentences.zh: 蜀之親族姻舊相依者數十家，希得廩之終身，昏喪悉損己力，晚年計口授田，各有差。

translations.literal: Several tens of families among his Sichuan kin, affines, and old associates depended on him; Xide provisioned them for life; weddings and funerals he wholly bore from his own strength; in his later years he counted mouths and granted fields, each with its allotment.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen Sichuan kin and old associates relied on him; Xide supported them for life, paid for every wedding and funeral himself, and in old age allotted fields by household, each according to need.

sentences.zh: 所著有《續言行錄》、《奏稿》、《橘州文集》。

translations.literal: His writings include Continued Records of Words and Deeds, Memorial Drafts, and Collected Works of Juzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Continued Records of Words and Deeds, Memorial Drafts, and Collected Works of Juzhou.

sentences.zh: 包恢，字宏父，建昌人。

translations.literal: Bao Hui, style Hongfu, was a man of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Hui, style Hongfu, was from Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 自其父揚、世父約、叔父遜從朱熹、陸九淵學。

translations.literal: From his father Yang, his father’s elder brother Yue, and his father’s younger brother Xun, he studied with Zhu Xi and Lu Jiuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yang, his uncle Yue, and his uncle Xun had studied with Zhu Xi and Lu Jiuyuan.

sentences.zh: 恢少為諸父門人講《大學》，其言高明，諸父驚焉。

translations.literal: Hui in youth lectured on the Great Learning to his uncles’ disciples; his words were lofty and clear, and the uncles were startled.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Hui lectured on the Great Learning to his uncles’ students; his exposition was so penetrating that they were astonished.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十三年，舉進士。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiading he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiading year 13 he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 調金谿主簿。

translations.literal: He was assigned as registrar of Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed registrar of Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 邵武守王遂辟光澤主簿，平寇亂。

translations.literal: Shaowu prefect Wang Sui recruited him as registrar of Guangze and he pacified bandit turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowu prefect Wang Sui recruited him as registrar of Guangze, where he pacified bandit unrest.

sentences.zh: 建寧守袁甫薦為府學教授，監虎翼軍，募土豪討唐石之寇。

translations.literal: Jianning prefect Yuan Fu recommended him as prefectural school instructor; he supervised the Tiger Wing Army, recruited local strongmen, and attacked the Tangshi bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Jianning prefect Yuan Fu recommended him as prefectural school instructor; he supervised the Tiger Wing Army, recruited local militia, and suppressed the Tangshi bandits.

sentences.zh: 授掌故，改沿海製置司幹官。

translations.literal: He was appointed archivist and changed to staff officer of the coastal commissionerate.
translations.idiomatic: He was made archivist, then staff officer of the coastal commissionerate.

sentences.zh: 會歲饑，盜起金壇、溧陽之間，恢部諸將為十誅夷之。

translations.literal: It happened that the year was famine-struck and bandits rose between Jintan and Liyang; Hui deployed the generals in ten groups and exterminated them.
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year bandits rose between Jintan and Liyang; Hui sent his generals in ten columns and exterminated them.

sentences.zh: 沿江製置使陳韡辟為機宜，復有平寇功，改知吉州永豐縣，未行，差發運幹官。

translations.literal: Yangtze coastal commissioner Chen Wei recruited him as confidential staff; again he had merit in pacifying bandits; he was changed to magistrate of Yongfeng in Jizhou but did not go; he was assigned as transport staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal commissioner Chen Wei made him confidential staff; after further success against bandits he was named magistrate of Yongfeng in Jizhou but did not take up the post and was assigned transport staff officer instead.

sentences.zh: 福建安撫使陳塏檄平寇，遷武學諭、宗正寺主簿，添差通判台州。

translations.literal: Fujian pacification commissioner Chen Kai ordered him to pacify bandits; he was moved to instructor of the Military School and registrar of the Imperial Clan Court, with supernumerary concurrent service as vice prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian pacification commissioner Chen Kai ordered him to pacify bandits; he was promoted to Military School instructor and Imperial Clan registrar, with supernumerary duty as vice prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 徐鹿卿討溫寇，辟兼提點刑獄司主管文字，議收捕。

translations.literal: Xu Luqing campaigned against Wenzhou bandits and recruited him to concurrently manage documents for the judicial intendant’s office, deliberating on rounding up and capture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Luqing campaigned against Wenzhou bandits and recruited him to manage documents for the judicial intendant, planning their capture.

sentences.zh: 改通判臨安府，遷宗正寺主簿、知台州。

translations.literal: He was changed to vice prefect of Lin’an, then moved to registrar of the Imperial Clan Court and prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice prefect of Lin’an, then Imperial Clan registrar and prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 有妖僧居山中，號“活佛”，男女爭事之，因為奸利，豪貴風靡，恢誅其僧。

translations.literal: There was a sorcerer-monk dwelling in the mountains styled the “Living Buddha”; men and women vied to serve him, and thereby he gained illicit profit; the powerful and noble were swept along; Hui executed the monk.
translations.idiomatic: A sorcerer-monk in the mountains called himself the “Living Buddha”; men and women flocked to him for illicit gain, and the gentry followed the fashion until Hui executed him.

sentences.zh: 進左司郎官，未行，改湖北提點刑獄，未行，移福建兼知建寧。

translations.literal: He was advanced to left bureau director; he did not go; he was changed to Hubei judicial intendant; he did not go; he was transferred to Fujian, concurrently prefect of Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to left bureau director, he did not take up the post; named Hubei judicial intendant, he again did not go; he was transferred to Fujian as concurrent prefect of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 閩俗以九月祠“五王”生日，靡金帛，傾市奉之。

translations.literal: Fujian custom in the ninth month sacrificed to the birthdays of the “Five Kings,” squandering gold and silk and emptying the market to serve them.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian custom held a ninth-month rite for the “Five Kings’” birthdays, squandering gold and silk as the whole market turned out to worship.

sentences.zh: 恢曰：“彼非犬豕，安得一日而五子同生，非不祥者乎？

translations.literal: Hui said: “They are not dogs or swine—how could five sons be born on one day? Is this not inauspicious?”
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, “They are not dogs or swine—how could five sons be born on one day? Is that not an ill omen?”

sentences.zh: 而尊畏之若是。

translations.literal: “Yet you honor and fear them to this degree.”
translations.idiomatic: “Yet you honor and fear them like this.”

sentences.zh: ”眾感悟，為之衰止。

translations.literal: ” The crowd was awakened and for this reason the practice declined and ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd took his point and the rite dwindled away.

sentences.zh: 兼轉運判官，以侍御史周坦論罷。

translations.literal: He was concurrently transport commissioner-assistant and was dismissed on impeachment by attendant censor Zhou Tan.
translations.idiomatic: As concurrent transport commissioner-assistant he was impeached and dismissed by attendant censor Zhou Tan.

sentences.zh: 光州布衣陳景夏上書云：“包恢剛正不屈之臣，言者汙蔑之耳。

translations.literal: Guangzhou commoner Chen Jingxia submitted a memorial saying: “Bao Hui is a minister upright and unbending; the speakers have only slandered him.”
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou commoner Chen Jingxia memorialized, “Bao Hui is an upright, unyielding minister; his critics have only slandered him.”

sentences.zh: ”又四年，起為廣東轉運判官，權經略使，遷侍右郎官，尋為大理少卿，即日除直顯文閣、浙西提點刑獄。

translations.literal: ” After another four years he was raised as Guangdong transport commissioner-assistant and acting pacification commissioner, moved to right attendant director, soon made vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, and the same day removed as direct associate of the Xianwen Pavilion and Zhexi judicial intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he was recalled as Guangdong transport commissioner-assistant and acting pacification commissioner, promoted to right attendant director, soon vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, and the same day made direct associate of the Xianwen Pavilion and Zhexi judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 是時海寇為亂，恢單車就道、調許、澉浦分屯建砦，一旦集諸軍討平之。

translations.literal: At this time sea bandits were in turmoil; Hui went alone in a single carriage on the road, deployed garrisons at Xu and Ganpu, and in one day gathered all armies and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Sea bandits were then in revolt; Hui went alone, stationed troops at Xu and Ganpu, and in one day gathered the armies and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 嘉興吏因和糴受賕百萬，恢被旨慮囚，曰：“吾用此消沴氣。

translations.literal: A Jiaxing clerk took a bribe of one million in connection with regulated grain purchase; Hui received an edict to review prisoners and said: “I use this to dispel baleful vapors.”
translations.idiomatic: A Jiaxing clerk took a million in bribes over regulated grain purchases; ordered to review prisoners, Hui said, “I will use this to dispel corruption.”

sentences.zh: ”乃減死，斷其手。

translations.literal: ” He then reduced the death sentence and cut off his hand.
translations.idiomatic: He commuted the death sentence and cut off the man’s hand.

sentences.zh: 進直龍圖閣、權發運，升秘閣修撰，知隆興府兼江西轉運。

translations.literal: He was advanced to direct associate of the Longtu Pavilion, acting transport commissioner, promoted to Privy Archives compiler, and made prefect of Longxing, concurrently Jiangxi transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to direct associate of the Longtu Pavilion and acting transport commissioner, then Privy Archives compiler, prefect of Longxing, and Jiangxi transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 沈妖妓於水，化為狐，人皆神之。

translations.literal: He drowned a sorceress in the water; she transformed into a fox, and all regarded it as divine.
translations.idiomatic: He drowned a sorceress in the river; she was said to turn into a fox, and people took it as miraculous.

sentences.zh: 有母訴子者，年月後狀作“疏”字，恢疑之，呼其子至，泣不言。

translations.literal: A mother sued her son; in the date on the plaint the character for “close” was written as “estranged”; Hui grew suspicious, summoned the son, who wept and would not speak.
translations.idiomatic: A mother sued her son; in the date on the plaint the character for “close” was written as “estranged”; Hui grew suspicious, summoned the son, who wept and would not speak.

sentences.zh: 及得其情，母孀居，與僧通，惡其子諫，以不孝坐之，狀則僧為之也。

translations.literal: When he obtained the facts, the mother lived as a widow and had relations with a monk; she hated her son’s remonstrance and had him convicted on unfilial conduct; the plaint had been written by the monk.
translations.idiomatic: The truth was that the widowed mother was carrying on with a monk, hated her son’s warnings, and had him charged with unfilial conduct on a plaint the monk had drafted.

sentences.zh: 因責子侍養跬步不離，僧無由至。

translations.literal: He therefore charged the son to attend and support her, not leaving her side for a single step, so the monk had no means to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the son to wait on her and never leave her side, so the monk could not come near.

sentences.zh: 母乃托夫諱日，入寺作佛事，以籠盛衣帛，因納僧於內以歸。

translations.literal: The mother then used her husband’s taboo day as a pretext, entered the temple to perform Buddhist rites, used a cage to hold clothing and silk, and thereby put the monk inside and brought him home.
translations.idiomatic: The mother used her husband’s death anniversary to enter a temple for Buddhist rites, hid clothing in a basket, and smuggled the monk home inside it.

sentences.zh: 恢知之，使人要之，置籠公庫，逾旬，吏報籠中臭達於外，恢命沉於江，語其子曰：“為汝除此害矣。

translations.literal: Hui knew of it and sent men to intercept them, placing the cage in the public storehouse; after more than ten days a clerk reported the stench from within the cage reached outside; Hui ordered it sunk in the river and told the son: “I have removed this harm for you.”
translations.idiomatic: Hui learned of it, had them intercepted, and put the basket in the government storehouse; after ten days clerks reported the stench spreading outside; Hui ordered it sunk in the river and told the son, “I have removed this scourge for you.”

sentences.zh: ”又姑死者假子婦棺以斂，家貧不能償，婦於恢，恢怒，買一棺，紿其婦臥棺中以試，就掩而葬之。

translations.literal: ” Again, when an aunt died she borrowed her son’s wife’s coffin for encoffinment; the family was poor and could not repay; the daughter-in-law appealed to Hui; Hui was angry, bought a coffin, deceived the daughter-in-law into lying in the coffin on the pretext of a trial fit, and at once covered and buried her.
translations.idiomatic: When an aunt died she borrowed her daughter-in-law’s coffin; the family was too poor to replace it, and the daughter-in-law appealed to Hui. Enraged, he bought a coffin, tricked her into lying in it “to try the fit,” and had it sealed and buried at once.

sentences.zh: 改湖南轉運使，罷。

translations.literal: He was changed to Hunan transport commissioner and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Hunan transport commissioner and then dismissed.

sentences.zh: 景定初，拜大理卿、樞密都承旨兼侍講，權禮部侍郎，尋為中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingding he was appointed director of the Court of Judicial Review, chief bearer of the Bureau of Military Affairs, concurrently lecturer, acting vice minister of Rites, and soon made drafter of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingding he was made director of the Court of Judicial Review, chief bearer of the Bureau of Military Affairs, lecturer, acting vice minister of Rites, and soon Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 林希逸奏恢守法奉公，其心如水。

translations.literal: Lin Xiyi memorialized that Hui observed the law and served the public; his mind was like water.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Xiyi memorialized that Hui upheld the law and served the public with a mind clear as water.

sentences.zh: 權刑部侍郎，進華文閣直學士、知平江府兼發運。

translations.literal: He was acting vice minister of Justice, advanced to Huawen Pavilion academician, prefect of Pingjiang, concurrently transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: As acting vice minister of Justice he was promoted to Huawen Pavilion academician, prefect of Pingjiang, and transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 豪有奪民包舉田寄公租誣上者，恢上疏，指為以小民祈天永命之一事，帝覽奏惻然，罪任事者，即歸民田。

translations.literal: A powerful man seized the people’s tax-contracted fields, registered them as public rent, and deceived the throne; Hui submitted a memorial, pointing to this as a matter in which the little people pray Heaven for enduring mandate; the emperor reading the memorial was deeply moved, punished those in charge, and at once returned the people’s fields.
translations.idiomatic: A magnate had seized commoners’ tax-contract fields, registered them as public rent, and deceived the court; Hui memorialized that this struck at the people’s plea to Heaven for enduring mandate. The emperor was deeply moved, punished the officials involved, and immediately returned the land.

sentences.zh: 召赴闕，辭，改知紹興，又辭。

translations.literal: He was summoned to court, declined, was changed to prefect of Shaoxing, and again declined.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, he declined; named prefect of Shaoxing, he declined again.

sentences.zh: 度宗即位，召為刑部尚書，進端明殿學士，簽書樞密院事，封南城縣侯。

translations.literal: When Duzong took the throne he was summoned as minister of Justice, advanced to Duanming Hall academician, deputy signer of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Nancheng County.
translations.idiomatic: When Duzong succeeded he was summoned as minister of Justice, made Duanming Hall academician and deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Nancheng.

sentences.zh: 郊祀禮成，還，以資政殿學士致仕。

translations.literal: When the suburban sacrifice rites were completed he returned and retired as Zizheng Hall academician.
translations.idiomatic: After the suburban sacrifice he returned and retired as Zizheng Hall academician.

sentences.zh: 恢曆仕所至，破豪猾，去奸吏，治蠱獄，課盆鹽，理銀欠，政聲赫然。

translations.literal: Wherever Hui served through his career, he broke powerful scoundrels, removed corrupt clerks, tried witchcraft cases, assessed basin salt, and settled silver arrears; his governmental reputation blazed.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served, Hui broke powerful bullies, removed corrupt clerks, tried witchcraft cases, assessed basin salt, and cleared silver arrears; his reputation for governance was resounding.

sentences.zh: 嚐因輪對曰：“此臣心惻隱所以深切為陛下告者，陛下惻隱之心如天地日月，其閉而食之者曰近習、曰外戚耳。

translations.literal: He once said at rotation audience: “This is what my heart’s compassion deeply urges me to tell Your Majesty: Your Majesty’s compassionate heart is like heaven and earth, sun and moon; those who shut it in and devour it are called intimate attendants and maternal kin, that is all.”
translations.idiomatic: At rotation audience he once said, “What my heart most urgently tells Your Majesty is this: your compassionate heart is like heaven and earth, sun and moon; those who shut it in and feed on it are your intimate attendants and your in-laws, nothing more.”

sentences.zh: ”參知政事董槐見而歎曰：“吾等有慚色矣。

translations.literal: ” Participant in governance Dong Huai, seeing it, sighed and said: “We have the color of shame.”
translations.idiomatic: Vice grand councilor Dong Huai read it and sighed, “We ought to blush.”

sentences.zh: ”他日講官因稱恢疏剴切，願容納。

translations.literal: ” Another day a lecturer cited Hui’s memorial as earnest and cutting and wished it might be received.
translations.idiomatic: Another day a lecturer praised Hui’s memorial as earnest and urged the emperor to heed it.

sentences.zh: 理宗欣然曰：“其言甚直，朕何嚐怒直言！

translations.literal: Emperor Lizong said with pleasure: “His words are very straight; when have I ever been angry at straight speech!”
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Lizong said gladly, “His words are very blunt—when have I ever been angry at blunt speech!”

sentences.zh: ”經筵奏對，誠實懇惻，至身心之要，未嚐不從容諄至。

translations.literal: ” At the classics mat in memorial and response he was sincere, earnest, and compassionate; on essentials of body and mind he never failed to be unhurried, thorough, and repeated.
translations.idiomatic: At the classics mat his answers were sincere and earnest; on matters touching body and mind he was always patient and thorough.

sentences.zh: 度宗至比恢為程顥、程頤。

translations.literal: Duzong even compared Hui to Cheng Hao and Cheng Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Duzong even compared Hui to Cheng Hao and Cheng Yi.

sentences.zh: 恢侍其父疾，滌濯拚除之役不命僮仆。

translations.literal: Hui attended his father’s illness; washing, scrubbing, and sweeping he did not command servants.
translations.idiomatic: When his father was ill Hui washed, scrubbed, and swept without calling servants.

sentences.zh: 年八十有七，臨終，舉盧懷慎臥簀窮約事戒諸子斂以深衣，作書別親戚而後卒，有光隕其地。

translations.literal: At age eighty-seven, on the verge of death, he cited Lu Huaishen’s lying on rush mats in poverty and restraint to admonish his sons to encoffin him in deep garments, wrote letters of farewell to kin, and afterward died; a light fell at that place.
translations.idiomatic: At eighty-seven, dying, he cited Lu Huaishen’s straw mat and plain coffin to warn his sons to bury him in simple deep garments, wrote farewell letters to kin, and died; a light was seen to fall there.

sentences.zh: 遺表聞，帝輟朝，贈少保，諡文肅，賻銀絹五百。

translations.literal: When his death memorial was heard, the emperor halted court, posthumously granted Junior Guardian, gave the posthumous title Wensu, and bestowed five hundred in silver and silk as funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When his final memorial arrived the emperor halted court, posthumously made him Junior Guardian, gave the posthumous title Wensu, and granted five hundred in silver and silk.

sentences.zh: 常挺字方叔，福州人。

translations.literal: Chang Ting, style Fangshu, was a man of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Ting, style Fangshu, was from Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙二年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the second year of Jiaxi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Jiaxi year 2.

sentences.zh: 曆官為太學錄，召試館職，遷秘書省正字兼莊文府教授，升校書郎。

translations.literal: Through offices he served as recorder of the Imperial Academy, was summoned to examination for archive posts, was moved to rectifier of the Secretariat concurrently instructor of the Zhuangwen Palace, and was promoted to collator.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Imperial Academy recorder, passed the archive examination, became Secretariat rectifier and Zhuangwen Palace instructor, and was promoted to collator.

sentences.zh: 輪對，乞以李若水配享高宗。

translations.literal: At rotation audience he begged that Li Ruoshui be granted associated sacrifice with Emperor Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: At rotation audience he asked that Li Ruoshui be granted associated sacrifice in Gaozong’s temple.

sentences.zh: 改秘書郎兼考功郎官，出知衢州，拜監察御史兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: He was changed to Secretariat secretary, concurrently officer of the Ministry of Personnel’s merit section, went out as prefect of Quzhou, and was appointed investigating censor, concurrently lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He became Secretariat secretary with concurrent duty in the Personnel Ministry’s merit section, went out as prefect of Quzhou, and was made investigating censor and lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 疏言邊閫三事：曰辟實才，曰奏實功，曰招實兵。

translations.literal: In a memorial he spoke on three matters for frontier command: namely recruiting real talent, reporting real merit, and recruiting real troops.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he urged three reforms for frontier command: recruit real talent, report real merit, and recruit real troops.

sentences.zh: 朝廷二事：曰選良吏，曰擢正人。

translations.literal: For the court, two matters: namely selecting good officials, namely promoting upright men.
translations.idiomatic: For the central government he urged two priorities: appoint capable officials and elevate men of integrity.

sentences.zh: 又言：“願陛下深思宏遠之規模，奮發清明之誌氣，立綱陳紀必為萬世之法程，昭德塞違以示百官之憲度。

translations.literal: He also said: “I hope Your Majesty will deeply ponder far-reaching designs, stir up clear and enlightened resolve, establish frameworks and set forth regulations that must serve as models for ten thousand generations, display virtue and block transgression to show the statutes for the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged: “Your Majesty should ponder designs of lasting scope and rouse a spirit of clarity; lay down frameworks and regulations fit to govern ten thousand generations, display virtue and shut out wrongdoing, and thereby set the standard for every office.”

sentences.zh: ”遷太常少卿兼國子司業，兼國史編修、實錄檢討兼直舍人院。

translations.literal: ” He was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Sacrifices, concurrently Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, concurrently compiler of the national history and collator of the veritable records, and holder of the Imperial Drafting Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Vice Director of the Court of Sacrifices and of the Directorate of Education, and concurrently compiler of the national history, collator of the veritable records, and holder of the Imperial Drafting Academy.

sentences.zh: 遷起居郎，權工部侍郎兼直學士院。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Diarist, acting Vice Minister of Works with concurrent Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Diarist, with acting appointment as Vice Minister of Works and concurrent duty in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 遷工部侍郎、給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Works and Attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Minister of Works and Attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 右諫議大夫陳堯道論罷。

translations.literal: He was dismissed on the remonstrance of Right Remonstrance Counselor Chen Yaodao.
translations.idiomatic: Right Remonstrance Counselor Chen Yaodao remonstrated against him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 以寶章閣直學士知漳州，改知泉州，權兵部尚書兼侍讀，權禮部尚書兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰。

translations.literal: As Academician of the Baozhang Pavilion he was made prefect of Zhangzhou, then transferred to prefect of Quanzhou, acting Minister of War with concurrent Reader-in-waiting, acting Minister of Rites with concurrent co-compiler of the national history and veritable records.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Baozhang Pavilion academician and prefect of Zhangzhou, then Quanzhou; he held acting appointments as Minister of War and Reader-in-waiting, then as Minister of Rites with concurrent co-compiler of the national history and veritable records.

sentences.zh: 進《帝學發題》，遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He presented Imperial Learning: Essay Topics and was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted Imperial Learning: Essay Topics and was promoted to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳三年，授同知樞密院事兼權參知政事，封合沙郡公，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianchun he was appointed Vice Director of the Privy Council with concurrent acting Vice Grand Councilor, enfeoffed as Duke of Heshha Commandery, and appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianchun year 3 he became Vice Director of the Privy Council and acting Vice Grand Councilor, was enfeoffed Duke of Heshha Commandery, and received appointment as Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 四年，致仕，尋卒，贈少保。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he retired from office; soon after he died and was posthumously given Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he retired; he died soon afterward and was posthumously honored as Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 陳宗禮字立之。

translations.literal: Chen Zongli, style Lizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zongli, style Lizhi.

sentences.zh: 少貧力學，袁甫為江東提點刑獄，宗禮往問學焉。

translations.literal: In youth he was poor and studied diligently; when Yuan Fu was Jiangdong judicial intendant, Zongli went to seek learning from him.
translations.idiomatic: Poor in youth, he studied hard; when Yuan Fu served as Jiangdong judicial intendant, Zongli went to study under him.

sentences.zh: 淳祐四年，舉進士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunyou he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunyou year 4 he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 調邵武軍判官，入為國子正，遷太學博士、國子監丞，轉秘書省著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He was assigned as judge of Shaowu Circuit, entered service as Rectifier of the Directorate of Education, was moved to Erudite of the Imperial Academy and Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, and was transferred to Assistant Compiler of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judge of Shaowu Circuit, then entered the capital as Directorate rectifier, became Imperial Academy erudite and Directorate vice director, and was transferred to Secretariat assistant compiler.

sentences.zh: 入對，言火不循軌。

translations.literal: Received in audience, he spoke that fire was not following its course.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he warned that fire was straying from its proper path—a celestial omen.

sentences.zh: 帝以星變為憂，宗禮曰：“上天示戒，在陛下修德布政以回天意。

translations.literal: The emperor was troubled by stellar anomalies; Zongli said: “Heaven is showing a warning—the matter lies in Your Majesty cultivating virtue and spreading good government to turn back Heaven’s intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was anxious about unusual stars; Zongli said, “Heaven is warning us. Your Majesty must cultivate virtue and govern well to move Heaven’s heart back to favor.”

sentences.zh: ”又曰：“天下方事於利欲之中，士大夫奔競趨利，惟至公可以遏之。

translations.literal: ” He also said: “The realm is now absorbed in profit and desire; scholar-officials rush and compete for gain—only utmost fairness can check this.
translations.idiomatic: He added, “The empire is caught up in profit and desire; officials scramble for gain. Only absolute fairness can restrain it.”

sentences.zh: ”兼考功郎官，兼國史實錄院校勘，兼景獻府教授，升著作郎，遷尚左郎官兼右司。

translations.literal: ” He was concurrently officer of the merit section, concurrently collator of the national history and veritable records, concurrently instructor of the Jingxian Palace, was promoted to Compiler, and was moved to Left Department officer with concurrent Right Department duty.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently in the merit section, as collator of the national history and veritable records, and as instructor of the Jingxian Palace; he was promoted to compiler, then became Left Department officer with concurrent Right Department duty.

sentences.zh: 時丁大全擅國柄，以言為諱。

translations.literal: At the time Ding Daquan monopolized state power and made speech taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Daquan then held sole sway over government and treated frank speech as forbidden.

sentences.zh: 宗禮歎曰：“此可一日居乎！

translations.literal: Zongli sighed and said: “How can one dwell here even a single day!
translations.idiomatic: Zongli sighed, “How can one stay in such a court even a day longer?

sentences.zh: ”陛對，言：“願為宗社大計，毋但為倉廩府庫之小計；

translations.literal: ” At palace audience he said: “I hope to act for the great design of altars and state, not only for the petty reckonings of granaries and treasuries;
translations.idiomatic: At palace audience he urged, “Act for the altars of state and the realm’s long survival, not merely for granaries and treasuries;

sentences.zh: 願得天下四海之心，毋但得左右便嬖戚畹之心；

translations.literal: I hope to win the hearts of all under Heaven within the four seas, not only the hearts of those at hand, favorites, consort kin, and affinal kin;
translations.idiomatic: win the hearts of the whole empire, not only those of attendants, favorites, and consort kin;

sentences.zh: 願寄腹心於忠良，毋但寄耳目於卑近；

translations.literal: I hope to entrust one’s inmost heart to the loyal and good, not only one’s eyes and ears to the base and near;
translations.idiomatic: entrust your inner counsel to the loyal and worthy, not your eyes and ears to the low and near at hand;

sentences.zh: 願四通八達以來正人，毋但旁蹊曲徑類引貪濁。

translations.literal: I hope to bring upright men through roads reaching in all directions, not only through side paths and crooked byways to draw in the greedy and corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: and bring upright men by open highways, not by back alleys that recruit the greedy and corrupt.”

sentences.zh: ”拜太常少卿，以直寶謨閣、廣東提點刑獄進直煥章閣，遷秘書監。

translations.literal: ” He was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Sacrifices; as holder of the Baomo Pavilion and Guangdong judicial intendant he was advanced to holder of the Huanzhang Pavilion, and was transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director of the Court of Sacrifices, advanced from Baomo Pavilion academician and Guangdong judicial intendant to Huanzhang Pavilion academician, and then became Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以監察御史虞慮言追兩官，送永州居住。

translations.literal: On the words of investigating censor Yu Lü he was stripped of two ranks and sent to reside at Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Yu Lü denounced him; he was stripped of two ranks and exiled to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 景定四年，拜侍御史，直龍圖閣、淮西轉運判官，遷刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingding he was appointed Attending Censor, holder of the Dragon Diagram Hall and Huai West transport vice commissioner, and was transferred to Minister of Justice.
