translations.idiomatic: In Jingding year 4 he became Attending Censor, Dragon Diagram Hall academician and Huai West transport vice commissioner, and was promoted to Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 以起居舍人曹孝慶言罷。

translations.literal: He was dismissed on the words of Diarist-attendant Cao Xiaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Diarist-attendant Cao Xiaoqing remonstrated against him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 度宗即位，兼侍講，拜殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Duzong took the throne, he was made concurrent Lecturer and appointed Palace Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Duzong acceded, he was made concurrent lecturer and Palace Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 疏言：“恭儉之德自上躬始，清白之規自宮禁始，左右之言利者必斥，蹊隧之私獻者必誅。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: “The virtue of respect and frugality must begin from Your Majesty’s own person; rules of purity must begin from within the palace; those at hand who speak of profit must be expelled, and private offerings through side paths and hidden ways must be punished.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote, “Respect and frugality must begin with Your Majesty; purity must begin in the inner palace. Banish attendants who urge profit, and punish secret gifts brought through back channels.”

sentences.zh: ”以《詩》進講，因奏：“帝王舉動，無微不顯，古人所以貴於慎獨也。

translations.literal: ” Lecturing on the Book of Songs, he further memorialized: “A ruler’s conduct—nothing slight fails to show itself; this is why the ancients prized being cautious in solitude.
translations.idiomatic: Lecturing on the Book of Songs, he added, “A ruler’s every act, however small, shows itself in the end. That is why the ancients prized vigilance even when alone.”

sentences.zh: ”權禮部侍郎兼給事中。

translations.literal: ” He was acting Vice Minister of Rites with concurrent Attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting Vice Minister of Rites and Attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 進讀《孝宗聖訓》，因奏：“安危治亂，常起於一念慮之間，念慮少差，禍亂隨見。

translations.literal: Reading aloud Emperor Xiaozong’s Sacred Instructions, he further memorialized: “Safety and danger, order and chaos, often arise within a single thought; if thought strays slightly, calamity and disorder follow at once.
translations.idiomatic: Reading Xiaozong’s Sacred Instructions, he said, “Order and chaos often begin in a single thought. Stray slightly in intent, and disaster follows at once.

sentences.zh: 天下之亂未有不起於微而成於著。

translations.literal: There has never been disorder under Heaven that did not begin in what was slight and become what was manifest.
translations.idiomatic: No empire has ever fallen to chaos that did not start small and grow plain to see.”

sentences.zh: ”又言：“不以私意害公法，乃國家之福。

translations.literal: ” He also said: “Not letting private intent harm public law—this is the state’s blessing.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, “The state is blessed when private whim does not damage public law.”

sentences.zh: ”帝曰：“孝宗家法，惟賞善罰惡為尤謹。

translations.literal: ” The emperor said: “In Xiaozong’s household law, rewarding good and punishing evil was especially strict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, “In Xiaozong’s household way, rewarding good and punishing evil were especially strict.”

sentences.zh: ”宗禮言：“有功不賞，有罪不罰，雖堯舜不能治天下，信不可不謹也。”

translations.literal: ” Zongli said: “If merit goes unrewarded and guilt goes unpunished, even Yao and Shun could not govern all under Heaven—truly this cannot but be kept strict.”
translations.idiomatic: Zongli replied, “Without rewarding merit or punishing guilt, even Yao and Shun could not rule the realm. This truly cannot be neglected.”

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎，尋權禮部尚書，乞奉祠，帝曰：“豈朕不足與有為耶？

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites, soon acting Minister of Rites; he begged a temple sinecure. The emperor said: “Is it that I am not worth acting with?
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Minister of Rites, then acting Minister of Rites, and asked for a temple sinecure. The emperor said, “Do you think I am not worth serving?”

sentences.zh: ”以華文閣直學士知隆興府，再辭，依舊職與待次差遣。

translations.literal: ” As Academician of the Huawen Pavilion he was made prefect of Longxing; he declined again and was given his former rank with assignment awaiting the next vacancy.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Huawen Pavilion academician and prefect of Longxing, declined again, and kept his former rank pending the next assignment.

sentences.zh: 逾年，依舊職廣東經略安撫使兼知廣州，加端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事，尋兼權參知政事。

translations.literal: After more than a year, in his former rank he was made Guangdong pacification commissioner with concurrent prefect of Guangzhou, was given Academician of the Duanming Hall and Signing Secretary of the Privy Council, and soon was made concurrent acting Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he became Guangdong pacification commissioner and prefect of Guangzhou, was made Duanming Hall academician and Signing Secretary of the Privy Council, and soon acting Vice Grand Councilor as well.

sentences.zh: 疏奏：“國所以立，曰天命人心。

translations.literal: In a memorial he submitted: “What a state stands upon is called Heaven’s mandate and the people’s hearts.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote, “A state stands on Heaven’s mandate and the people’s hearts.

sentences.zh: 因其警而加敬畏，天命未有不可回也；

translations.literal: Taking warning from alarms and adding reverence and awe, Heaven’s mandate has never been such that it cannot be turned back;
translations.idiomatic: Heed warnings and grow reverent, and Heaven’s mandate may yet be turned;

sentences.zh: 因其未墜而加綏定，人心未嚐不可回也。

translations.literal: because it has not yet fallen and adding pacification and stability, the people’s hearts have never been such that they cannot be turned back.
translations.idiomatic: while the realm has not yet fallen, steady the people, and their hearts have never been beyond recall.”

sentences.zh: ”卒官，遺表上，贈開府儀同三司、盱江郡侯，諡文定。

translations.literal: ” He died in office; his final memorial was submitted. He was posthumously given Grand Preceptor with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, Marquis of Xujiang Commandery, with posthumous title Wendiing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; his final memorial reached the throne. He was posthumously honored Grand Preceptor of equal ceremonial rank to the Three Excellencies, Marquis of Xujiang Commandery, with the posthumous title Wendiing.

sentences.zh: 所著有《寄懷斐稿》、《曲轅散木集》、《兩朝奏議》、《經筵講義》、《經史明辨》、《經史管見》、《人物論》。

translations.literal: Works he authored include Drafts of Cherished Thoughts, Collected Writings of Crooked Axle and Scattered Timber, Memorials of Two Reigns, Lectures for the Classics Colloquium, Discriminations in Classics and History, Overview of Classics and History, and Discourses on Persons.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include Drafts of Cherished Thoughts, Collected Writings of Crooked Axle and Scattered Timber, Memorials of Two Reigns, Lectures for the Classics Colloquium, Discriminations in Classics and History, Overview of Classics and History, and Discourses on Persons.

sentences.zh: 常楙字長孺，顯謨閣直學士同之曾孫。

translations.literal: Chang Mao, style Changru, was great-grandson of Academician of the Xianmo Pavilion Chang Tongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Mao, style Changru, was the great-grandson of Xianmo Pavilion academician Chang Tongzhi.

sentences.zh: 入太學。

translations.literal: He entered the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 淳祐七年舉進士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chunyou he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunyou year 7 he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 調常熟尉。

translations.literal: He was assigned as assistant magistrate of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned assistant magistrate of Changshu.

sentences.zh: 公廉自持，不畏強禦，部使者交薦之。

translations.literal: Upright and incorrupt he held himself; he did not fear the powerful, and circuit envoys repeatedly recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and incorrupt, he did not fear the powerful; circuit envoys repeatedly recommended him.

sentences.zh: 調婺州推官。

translations.literal: He was assigned as investigating officer of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned investigating officer of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 疏決滯訟，以剸繁裁劇稱。

translations.literal: He cleared backlog lawsuits and was famed for cutting through complexity and judging heavy cases.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared backlog lawsuits and won renown for mastering complex and urgent cases.

sentences.zh: 臨安府尹馬光祖又薦於朝，辟差平江府百萬倉檢察，不受和糴事例，戢吏卒苛取。

translations.literal: Lin’an prefect Ma Guangzu again recommended him to court; he was specially assigned inspector of the Million-Granary of Pingjiang Prefecture, did not accept the quotas for state grain purchase, and restrained clerks and soldiers from harsh exactions.
translations.idiomatic: Lin’an prefect Ma Guangzu recommended him again; as inspector of Pingjiang’s Million-Granary he refused improper state-purchase quotas and curbed clerks’ and soldiers’ harsh exactions.

sentences.zh: 發運使趙與芮兼提點刑獄，屬楙檢核，雪無錫翟氏冤獄。

translations.literal: Transport commissioner Zhao Yuru concurrently served as judicial intendant and entrusted Mao to review cases, clearing the wrongful conviction of the Zhai clan of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioner and judicial intendant Zhao Yuru had Mao review cases and cleared the wrongful conviction of the Zhai family of Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 監江淮茶鹽所蕪湖局，不受商稅贏，光祖益敬之。

translations.literal: As superintendent of the Jiang-Huai Tea and Salt Office at Wuhu, he did not accept surplus merchant tax; Guangzu respected him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: As superintendent of the Jiang-Huai Tea and Salt bureau at Wuhu he refused excess merchant levies, and Guangzu respected him still more.

sentences.zh: 改知嘉定縣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be magistrate of Jiading County.
translations.idiomatic: He was made magistrate of Jiading County.

sentences.zh: 歲大水，勸分和糴，按籍均敷。

translations.literal: In a year of great flood he urged partition and state purchase of grain and distributed levies evenly according to registers.
translations.idiomatic: When flood struck he urged shared relief and state grain purchases, distributing burdens evenly by household register.

sentences.zh: 發運使王爚、提點刑獄孫子秀俱特薦於朝，簽書臨安府判官，不為權勢撓。

translations.literal: Transport commissioner Wang Can and judicial intendant Sun Zixiu both specially recommended him to court; as signing judge of Lin’an Prefecture he was not swayed by power.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Can and Sun Zixiu both specially recommended him; as signing judge of Lin’an he would not bend to powerful interests.

sentences.zh: 有為淮東提舉常平，辟楙提管，楙知其不可與共事，笑而卻之。

translations.literal: You Wei was Huai East intendant for the Ever-Normal Granaries and summoned Mao to oversee affairs; Mao knew he could not work with him, smiled, and declined.
translations.idiomatic: When You Wei, Huai East Ever-Normal intendant, summoned Mao to serve under him, Mao knew they could not work together and declined with a smile.

sentences.zh: 未幾，政府強楙行，遂拂衣去，朝野高之。

translations.literal: Before long the government forced Mao to go; he shook out his robes and left, and court and countryside honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the government forced him to accept; he resigned on the spot, and court and country held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 主管城南廂，聽訟嚴明，豪石益憚之。

translations.literal: As superintendent of the South City Ward he heard cases with stern clarity; powerful families feared him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: As superintendent of the South City Ward he heard cases with stern clarity, and local magnates feared him still more.

sentences.zh: 都城火後，瓦礫充斥，差民船徙運，在籍者百五十家，惟二十有五家應役，餘率為勢要宦官所庇。

translations.literal: After the capital fire rubble filled the streets; commoners’ boats were assigned to remove and transport it. Of one hundred fifty households on the register, only twenty-five answered corvée; the rest were mostly sheltered by powerful persons and eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital fire, rubble filled the streets and commoners’ boats were drafted to haul it away. Of 150 registered households only 25 performed service; the rest were shielded by powerful men and eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 楙悉追之，不服者杖其人，械於他所，無不聽命。

translations.literal: Mao pursued them all; those who would not obey he caned and shackled elsewhere—none failed to heed orders.
translations.idiomatic: Mao pursued them all; he caned resisters and shackled them elsewhere until every household obeyed.

sentences.zh: 又力拒戶部科買。

translations.literal: He also vigorously resisted the Ministry of Revenue’s requisition purchases.
translations.idiomatic: He also firmly resisted the Revenue Ministry’s forced purchases.

sentences.zh: 葉夢鼎、陳昉深期獎焉。

translations.literal: Ye Mengding and Chen Fang deeply looked to reward him.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Mengding and Chen Fang held him in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 添差臨安通判。

translations.literal: He was given an added assignment as vice prefect of Lin’an.
translations.idiomatic: He received an added assignment as vice prefect of Lin’an.

sentences.zh: 朝命鞫封樁庫吏範成獄，不肯承廟堂風旨，無辜者悉出之。

translations.literal: The court ordered him to try the case of sealed-reserve treasury clerk Fan Cheng; he would not accept the council chamber’s intent and released all who were innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to try sealed-reserve clerk Fan Cheng, he refused to follow the council’s bent and freed every innocent defendant.

sentences.zh: 知廣德軍。

translations.literal: He was made prefect of Guangde Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He became prefect of Guangde Circuit.

sentences.zh: 郡有水災，發社倉粟以活饑民，官吏難之，楙先發而後請專命之罪，置慈幼局，立先賢祠。

translations.literal: The commandery suffered flood; he released community-granary grain to save starving people. Officials objected; Mao released grain first and afterward begged punishment for acting without special authorization. He established a Bureau for Cherishing the Young and built a shrine to former sages.
translations.idiomatic: When flood struck the commandery he opened community granaries to feed the hungry. Officials hesitated; Mao released grain first, then asked to be punished for acting without authorization. He founded a charity bureau for orphans and built a shrine to former sages.

sentences.zh: 故事，郡守秋苗例可得米千石，乃以代屬縣償大農綱欠。

translations.literal: By precedent a commandery prefect’s autumn grain levy customarily yielded one thousand piculs of rice; he used this to repay on behalf of subordinate counties the shortfall in the grand grain transport quota.
translations.idiomatic: By custom a prefect’s autumn grain share was a thousand piculs of rice; he used it to cover subordinate counties’ shortfalls in the state grain transport quota.

sentences.zh: 拜監察御史，知無不言。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor and spoke without reserve on whatever he knew.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed investigating censor, he spoke without reserve on every matter he knew.

sentences.zh: 嚐論天變及賈似道家爭田事，論繼皇子竑嗣，觸度宗怒，遷司農卿，尋為兩浙轉運使。

translations.literal: He once spoke on celestial anomalies and on Jia Sidao’s family land dispute, and argued for succession by Prince Zi Qi—provoking Emperor Duzong’s anger; he was moved to Director of the Court of Agriculture and soon made transport commissioner of the Two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke on celestial omens and Jia Sidao’s land dispute, and urged succession for Prince Qi—angering Duzong, who transferred him to Director of the Court of Agriculture and soon made him Two Zhe transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 禁戢吏奸，不以急符督常賦。

translations.literal: He forbade and restrained clerks’ wrongdoing and did not use urgent orders to press regular levies.
translations.idiomatic: He curbed corrupt clerks and refused to press regular taxes with urgent orders.

sentences.zh: 海鹽歲為鹹潮害稼，楙請於朝，捐金發粟，復輟己帑，大加修築新塘三千六百二十五丈，名曰海晏塘。

translations.literal: In Haiyan salt fields each year brine tides harmed the crops; Mao petitioned court, donated funds and released grain, and again gave from his own purse, greatly repairing and building a new dyke of three thousand six hundred twenty-five zhang, named the Haiyan Dyke.
translations.idiomatic: Each year brine tides from the sea damaged Haiyan’s fields; Mao petitioned the court, donated funds and grain, and gave from his own purse to build a new dyke 3,625 zhang long, which he named the Calm Sea Dyke.

sentences.zh: 是秋，風濤大作，塘不浸者尺許，民得奠居，歲復告稔，邑人德之。

translations.literal: That autumn winds and waves rose greatly; the dyke was submerged by only a foot or so, the people were able to settle securely, the year again reported abundance, and the district people were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn fierce winds and waves struck; the dyke was flooded only a foot deep, the people kept their homes, the harvest was good again, and the district honored him.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 受四方民詞，務通下情。

translations.literal: He received petitions from the people of the four directions and strove to convey conditions below.
translations.idiomatic: He received petitions from across the realm and worked to bring the people’s concerns to the court.

sentences.zh: 兼中書門下省檢正諸房公事，兼刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was concurrently Rectifier of the Various Bureaus of the Secretariat-Chancellery and Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He concurrently rectified affairs in the Secretariat-Chancellery bureaus and served as Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 極論檢覆之敝。

translations.literal: He spoke at length on the abuses of review and verification.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke at length against abuses in fiscal review and verification.

sentences.zh: 上進故事，首論雷雪非時之變，帝意不悅。

translations.literal: He presented precedents to the throne, opening with untimely thunder and snow; the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting historical precedents to the throne, he began with untimely thunder and snow; the emperor took offense.

sentences.zh: 丐祠，不許，以集英殿修撰知平江。

translations.literal: He begged a temple sinecure; it was not granted, and he was made Compiler of the Jiying Hall and prefect of Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a temple sinecure but was refused; instead he was made Jiying Hall compiler and prefect of Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 值旱。

translations.literal: A drought occurred.
translations.idiomatic: A drought struck.

sentences.zh: 故事，郡守合得緡錢十五萬，悉以為民食、軍餉助。

translations.literal: By precedent a prefect was entitled to one hundred fifty thousand strings of cash; he used it all to aid the people’s food and military provisions.
translations.idiomatic: By custom a prefect was entitled to 150,000 strings of cash; he gave it all to feed the people and supply the troops.

sentences.zh: 蠲苗九萬、稅十三萬、版帳十六萬，又蠲新苗二萬八千，大寬公私之力。

translations.literal: He remitted ninety thousand in seed grain, one hundred thirty thousand in tax, one hundred sixty thousand in land-register levies, and again remitted twenty-eight thousand in new seed grain, greatly easing public and private burdens.
translations.idiomatic: He remitted 90,000 in seed grain, 130,000 in tax, and 160,000 in register levies, plus another 28,000 in new seed grain, greatly easing burdens on public and private alike.

sentences.zh: 飛蝗幾及境，疾風飄入太湖。

translations.literal: Locusts in flight nearly reached the border; a fierce wind blew them into Lake Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Locust swarms nearly reached the prefecture, but a fierce wind blew them into Lake Tai.

sentences.zh: 節浮費，修府庫。

translations.literal: He curbed extravagant spending and repaired the prefectural treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He cut wasteful spending and restored the prefectural treasury.

sentences.zh: 既代，有送還事例，自給吏卒外，餘金萬楮，楙悉不受。

translations.literal: After he was replaced, there was the precedent of send-back gifts; apart from provisions for clerks and soldiers, the remaining cash was ten thousand notes—all of which Mao refused.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office, custom allowed send-back gifts; beyond provisions for his staff, ten thousand notes remained—and Mao refused every one.

sentences.zh: 吏驚曰：“人言常侍郎不愛錢，果然。

translations.literal: A clerk exclaimed: “People say Vice Minister Chang does not love money—it is truly so.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk exclaimed, “People say Vice Minister Chang cares nothing for money—and it is true!

sentences.zh: ”改浙東安撫使。

translations.literal: ” He was transferred to Eastern Zhe pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Eastern Zhe pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 值水災，捐萬楮以振之，復請糴於朝，得米萬石，蠲新苗三萬八千。

translations.literal: Flood struck; he donated ten thousand notes for relief, again petitioned court for state purchase of grain and obtained ten thousand piculs of rice, and remitted thirty-eight thousand in new seed grain.
translations.idiomatic: When flood struck he donated ten thousand notes for relief, petitioned the court for grain purchases and obtained ten thousand piculs, and remitted 38,000 in new seed grain.

sentences.zh: 又以諸暨被水尤甚，給二萬楮付縣折運，民食不至乏絕。

translations.literal: Because Zhuji was especially hard hit by water, he gave twenty thousand notes to the county for transport conversion, so the people’s food did not run out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuji was hit especially hard; he gave the county twenty thousand notes for transport and conversion so the people did not go hungry.

sentences.zh: 民各祀於家。

translations.literal: The people each enshrined him in their homes.
translations.idiomatic: The people enshrined him in their homes.

sentences.zh: 兩浙及會稽、山陰死者暴露與貧而無以為殮者，乃以十萬楮置普惠庫，取息造棺以給之。

translations.literal: In the Two Zhe circuits and in Kuaiji and Shanyin, for the dead left exposed and the poor with no means for burial, he placed one hundred thousand notes in a Universal Benefit warehouse, took interest to make coffins, and supplied them.
translations.idiomatic: For the unburied dead and the poor who could not afford funerals in Two Zhe, Kuaiji, and Shanyin, he deposited 100,000 notes in a Universal Benefit warehouse and used the interest to provide coffins.

sentences.zh: 尋以刑部侍郎召。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 申明期赦敘改法，與廟堂爭可否，辨偽關獄，救八倉虧欠免死罪，平反天井巷殺人獄，全活者甚眾。

translations.literal: He clarified the law on scheduled amnesty and rank restoration, disputed with the council chamber over approval or rejection, distinguished a false customs case, saved those in the eight granaries’ deficits from the death penalty, reversed the wrongful murder case of Heavenly Well Lane, and many were wholly spared.
translations.idiomatic: He clarified the law on scheduled amnesty and rank restoration, disputed policy with the council, exposed a false customs case, spared granary officials facing death for deficits, reversed the Heavenly Well Lane murder conviction, and saved many lives.

sentences.zh: 兼給事中，封還隆國夫人從子黃進觀察使錄黃。

translations.literal: Concurrently Attendant-in-ordinary, he sealed and returned the commission for Lady of Long State’s nephew’s son Huang Jin as observation commissioner, returning the yellow edict.
translations.idiomatic: As concurrent Attendant-in-ordinary he sealed and returned the edict appointing Lady of Long State’s nephew’s son Huang Jin observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，似道以禦書令委曲書行，楙迄不奉命。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; Jia Sidao used an imperial letter ordering tactful drafting and execution, but Mao to the end would not obey the order.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious; Jia Sidao sent an imperial order to draft and execute the appointment tactfully, but Mao refused to the end.

sentences.zh: 以寶章閣待制提舉太平興國宮。

translations.literal: As Awaiting Draftsman of the Baozhang Pavilion he was made superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Baozhang Pavilion awaiting draftsman and superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Abbey.

sentences.zh: 德祐元年，拜吏部尚書，以老病辭，累詔不許，專官趣行甚峻。

translations.literal: In the first year of Deyou he was appointed Minister of Personnel; citing age and illness he declined, but repeated edicts would not permit it, and a special envoy was sent with stern urgency to hasten his departure.
translations.idiomatic: In Deyou year 1 he was appointed Minister of Personnel; he declined citing age and illness, but repeated edicts refused him, and a special envoy was sent with stern orders to hurry him to court.

sentences.zh: 楙入見，首言“霅川之變，非其本心，置之死，過矣，不與立後，又過矣。

translations.literal: Mao entered audience and spoke first: “The Shechuan affair was not his true intent; putting him to death was excessive, and not granting him a successor was excessive as well.
translations.idiomatic: At audience Mao spoke first: “The Shechuan affair was not Prince Qi’s true intent. Putting him to death was excessive; denying him an heir was excessive as well.

sentences.zh: 巴陵帝王之胄，生不得正命，死不得血食，沉冤幽憤，鬱結四五十年之久，不為妖為劄於冥冥中者幾希。

translations.literal: A scion of the Baling imperial house—in life he did not receive a proper fate, in death he did not receive blood offerings; his deep wrongs and hidden grief have been pent up for four or five decades. It is a wonder he has not become a demon or apparition in the dark realm.
translations.idiomatic: He was of the Baling imperial line: denied a proper fate in life and sacrificial offerings in death. Grievance and silent rage have festered for forty or fifty years; it is little short of a miracle that no demon or haunting spirit has risen from the shades.

sentences.zh: 願陛下勿搖浮議，特發神斷，宗社幸甚”。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will not be swayed by floating opinion but will issue a divine decision in special measure—the altars of state would be greatly fortunate.”
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty not to waver before loose talk, but to reach a decisive judgment on your own—the dynasty would be greatly blessed.”

sentences.zh: 於是詔國史院討論典故以聞。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the National History Academy to discuss precedents and report.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered the National History Academy to research precedents and report back.

sentences.zh: 明堂禮成，進端明殿學士、提領戶部財用，特與執政恩數。

translations.literal: When the Bright Hall rites were completed, he was advanced to Academician of the Duanming Hall and superintendent of Ministry of Revenue finances, and was specially granted the perquisites of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: After the Bright Hall ceremony he was promoted to Duanming Hall academician and put in charge of Ministry of Revenue finances, with the special perquisites granted to chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 楙以國步方艱，非臣子貪榮之時，力辭恩數。

translations.literal: Mao, because the state’s step was just then arduous, said it was not the time for subjects to covet glory, and strenuously declined the perquisites.
translations.idiomatic: Mao held that with the realm in crisis it was no hour for ministers to seek honor, and he firmly refused the special grants.

sentences.zh: 與廟堂議事不合，以疾謁告。

translations.literal: He did not agree with court deliberations and requested leave on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He fell out with court policy and took leave citing illness.

sentences.zh: 二年春，拜參知政事，為夏士林繳駁，拜疏出關，後六年卒。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor; Xia Shilin submitted a rejection, and he presented a memorial and left the pass; six years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year 2 he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor; Xia Shilin blocked the appointment, and Mao memorialized and left the capital. He died six years later.

sentences.zh: 家鉉翁，眉州人。

translations.literal: Jia Xuanweng was a native of Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xuanweng was from Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 以蔭補官。

translations.literal: Through yin privilege he received office.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office through hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 累官知常州，政譽翕然。

translations.literal: Through successive offices he became prefect of Changzhou; his administrative reputation flourished.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to prefect of Changzhou, where his governance won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 遷浙東提點刑獄，入為大理少卿，直華文閣，以秘閣修撰充紹興府長史，遷樞密都丞旨，知建寧府兼福建轉運副使，權戶部侍郎兼知臨安府、浙西安撫使，遷戶部侍郎，權侍右侍郎，仍兼樞密都丞旨。

translations.literal: He was transferred to judicial intendant of eastern Zhejiang, entered the capital as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, was attached to the Huawen Pavilion, served as chief administrator of Shaoxing prefecture as Secretariat compiler, was moved to chief clerk of the Privy Council, was prefect of Jianning with concurrent transport vice commissioner of Fujian, acting Vice Minister of Revenue with concurrent prefect of Lin’an and Zhexi Pacification Commissioner, was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue, acting Vice Minister of the Right with concurrent chief clerk of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: He became judicial intendant of eastern Zhejiang, then Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review in the capital and holder of the Huawen Pavilion; he served as Shaoxing chief administrator and Secretariat compiler, chief clerk of the Privy Council, prefect of Jianning with concurrent Fujian transport vice commissioner, acting Vice Minister of Revenue with concurrent prefect of Lin’an and Zhexi pacification commissioner, then Vice Minister of Revenue and acting Vice Minister of the Right, still holding the Privy Council chief clerkship.

sentences.zh: 賜進士出身，拜端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was granted jinshi status and appointed Academician of the Duanming Hall and signing clerk of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted jinshi standing and made Duanming Hall academician and signing clerk of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 大元兵次近郊，丞相吳堅、賈餘慶檄告天下守令以城降，鉉翁獨不署。

translations.literal: Great Yuan troops halted near the suburbs; Grand Councillors Wu Jian and Jia Yuqing issued a proclamation telling all prefects and magistrates in the realm to surrender their cities—Xuanweng alone would not sign.
translations.idiomatic: As Yuan forces camped near the capital, Grand Councillors Wu Jian and Jia Yuqing circulated a proclamation ordering every prefect and magistrate to surrender his city. Xuanweng alone refused to sign.

sentences.zh: 元帥遣使至，欲加縛，鉉翁曰：“中書省無縛執政之理。

translations.literal: The marshal sent envoys who wished to bind him; Xuanweng said: “In the Secretariat there is no precedent for binding a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The marshal sent men intending to bind him. Xuanweng said, “The Secretariat has no precedent for seizing a chief minister.

sentences.zh: ”堅奉表祈請於大元，以鉉翁介之，禮成不得命，留館中。

translations.literal: ” Jian presented a memorial of petition to the Great Yuan, using Xuanweng as envoy; when the rites were completed he received no dismissal and was kept in the lodge.
translations.idiomatic: ” Wu Jian submitted a petition to the Yuan court and sent Xuanweng as envoy. When the audience ended he was given no leave to depart and was detained in the guest lodge.

sentences.zh: 聞宋亡，旦夕哭泣不食飲者數月。

translations.literal: When he heard that Song had perished, for months he wept morning and evening and did not eat or drink.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Song had fallen, he wept day and night and took no food or drink for months.

sentences.zh: 大元以其節高欲尊官之，以示南服。

translations.literal: The Great Yuan, because his integrity was lofty, wished to honor him with high office to display this to the southern domains.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan court, admiring his integrity, wished to elevate him to high office as an example to the south.

sentences.zh: 鉉翁義不二君，辭無詭對。

translations.literal: Xuanweng, in righteousness, would not serve two rulers; in declining he had no evasive answers.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanweng would not betray his sovereign; in refusing office he gave no evasive reply.

sentences.zh: 宋三宮北還，鉉翁再率故臣迎謁，伏地流涕，頓首謝奉使無狀，不能感動上衷，無以保存其國。

translations.literal: When the three palaces of Song returned north, Xuanweng again led former ministers to meet and pay homage; prostrate on the ground he wept, knocked his head and apologized that as envoy he had been unworthy, unable to move the sovereign heart, unable to preserve the state.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song imperial household was sent north, Xuanweng again led former ministers to receive them. He prostrated himself, weeping, and kowtowed in apology: as envoy he had failed, could not move the emperor’s heart, and could not save the realm.

sentences.zh: 見者莫不歎息。

translations.literal: Those who saw it none failed to sigh.
translations.idiomatic: All who witnessed it sighed.

sentences.zh: 文天祥女弟坐兄故，係奚官，鉉翁傾橐中裝贖出之，以歸其兄璧。

translations.literal: Wen Tianxiang’s younger sister, implicated because of her brother, was held by a Xi official; Xuanweng emptied his purse to ransom her and returned her to her brother Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tianxiang’s sister, implicated in her brother’s case, was held by a Xi official. Xuanweng spent all he had to ransom her and sent her back to her brother Bi.

sentences.zh: 鉉翁狀貌奇偉，身長七尺，被服儼雅。

translations.literal: Xuanweng’s form was extraordinarily imposing; his body was seven chi in height, and his dress was solemn and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanweng was striking in appearance—seven chi tall, dressed with grave elegance.

sentences.zh: 其學邃於《春秋》，自號則堂，改館河間，乃以《春秋》教授弟子，數為諸生談宋故事及宋興亡之故，或流涕太息。

translations.literal: His learning was profound in the Spring and Autumn Annals; he styled himself Zetang. Transferred to lodge at Hejian, he thereupon used the Spring and Autumn Annals to instruct disciples, and often for the students spoke of Song stories and the causes of Song’s rise and fall—sometimes weeping and sighing deeply.
translations.idiomatic: He was a master of the Spring and Autumn Annals and took the style Zetang. Resettled at Hejian, he taught the classic to his pupils and often recounted Song history and the dynasty’s fall—sometimes weeping aloud.

sentences.zh: 大元成宗皇帝即位，放還，賜號“處士”，錫齎金幣，皆辭不受。

translations.literal: When Emperor Chengzong of the Great Yuan took the throne, he was released and granted the title “Recluse”; gold and coins were bestowed—all were declined and not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chengzong of Yuan succeeded, he was sent home and given the title Recluse, with gifts of gold and coin—all of which he refused.

sentences.zh: 又數年以壽終。

translations.literal: Several years later he died of old age.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later he died at an advanced age.

sentences.zh: 李庭芝，字祥甫。

translations.literal: Li Tingzhi, style Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tingzhi, style Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 其先汴人，十二世同居，號“義門李氏”，後徙隨之應山縣。

translations.literal: His ancestors were men of Bian; twelve generations dwelt together and were styled “the Li clan of the Righteous Gate”; later they moved to Yingshan County in Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears were from Bian. Twelve generations lived under one roof as the “Li clan of the Righteous Gate,” later moving to Yingshan in Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 金亡，襄、漢被兵，又徙隨。

translations.literal: When Jin perished, Xiang and Han were afflicted by troops, and they moved again to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin fell and Xiang and Han were ravaged by war, the family moved again to Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 然特以武顯。

translations.literal: Yet they were especially distinguished for martial achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The clan was known above all for military prowess.

sentences.zh: 庭芝生時，有芝產屋棟，鄉人聚觀，以為生男祥也，遂以名之。

translations.literal: When Tingzhi was born, fungus grew on the house ridge; villagers gathered to look on it and took it as an auspice of a male birth, and so named him.
translations.idiomatic: At his birth fungus appeared on the roof beam; neighbors gathered to see it as an omen of a son, and so he was named.

sentences.zh: 少穎異，日能誦數千言，而智識恒出長老之上。

translations.literal: In youth he was exceptionally bright; daily he could recite several thousand words, and his understanding constantly surpassed his elders.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was unusually gifted, reciting thousands of characters a day, and his judgment often outstripped his elders.

sentences.zh: 王旻守隨，庭芝年十八，告其諸父曰：“王公貪而不恤下，下多怨之，隨必亂，請徙家德安以避。

translations.literal: Wang Min guarded Sui; Tingzhi at eighteen told his uncles: “Lord Wang is greedy and does not care for those below; below there is much resentment—Sui will surely fall into disorder. Please move the family to De’an to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Min held Suizhou, the eighteen-year-old Tingzhi told his uncles, “Lord Wang is greedy and heedless of his men; they resent him. Suizhou will surely rebel. Move our household to De’an while we can.

sentences.zh: ”諸父勉強從之，未浹旬，旻果為部曲挾之以叛，隨民死者甚眾。

translations.literal: ” His uncles reluctantly followed; before ten days had passed, Min was indeed seized by his troops and carried off in rebellion, and very many people of Sui died.
translations.idiomatic: ” His uncles reluctantly agreed. Within ten days Wang Min’s troops had seized him and risen in revolt, and countless people of Suizhou perished.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙末，江防甚急，庭芝得鄉舉不行，以策幹荊帥孟珙請自效。

translations.literal: At the end of Jiaxi the river defense was very urgent; Tingzhi received the provincial recommendation but did not take office, and with a stratagem approached Jingnan commander Meng Gong begging to offer himself.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Jiaxi era, with river defense critical, Tingzhi passed the provincial examination but declined office and went to Jingnan commander Meng Gong with a plan, offering his service.

sentences.zh: 珙善相人，且夜夢車騎稱李尚書謁己，明日庭芝至。

translations.literal: Gong was skilled at physiognomy, and moreover by night dreamed of chariots and horsemen saying Vice Minister Li sought an audience; the next day Tingzhi arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Gong was skilled at reading faces and had dreamed that night of an entourage announcing that Vice Minister Li sought audience; the next day Tingzhi came.

sentences.zh: 珙見其魁偉，顧諸子曰：“吾相人多，無如李生者，其名位當過我。

translations.literal: Gong saw his imposing stature, turned to his sons and said: “I have read many faces, but none like this Li; his name and position should surpass mine.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Tingzhi’s imposing frame, Meng Gong told his sons, “I have judged many men, but none like this Li. His rank will exceed mine.

sentences.zh: ”時四川有警，即以庭芝權施之建始縣。

translations.literal: ” At that time Sichuan had an alarm, and Tingzhi was at once made acting magistrate of Jianshi in Shi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: ” Sichuan was then under threat, and Tingzhi was immediately appointed acting magistrate of Jianshi in Shi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 庭芝至，訓農治兵，選壯士雜官軍教之。

translations.literal: When Tingzhi arrived, he trained the farmers and managed the troops, selected stalwart men and mixed them with the regular army to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he trained farmers for war, selected strong men, and drilled them alongside regular troops.

sentences.zh: 期年，民皆知戰守，善馳逐，無事則植戈而耕，兵至則悉出而戰。

translations.literal: Within a year the people all knew defense and attack, were skilled at riding and pursuit; when there was no affair they planted spears and plowed, and when troops came they all went out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year every man knew how to fight: they farmed with spears at hand and turned out in full when the enemy came.

sentences.zh: 夔帥下其法於所部行之。

translations.literal: The Kuizhou commander spread his method through the districts under his command and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: The Kuizhou commander adopted his system throughout his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 淳祐初始去，舉進士，中第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunyou he first left office, took the jinshi examination, and passed.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chunyou era he left office, sat for the jinshi, and passed.

sentences.zh: 辟珙幕中，主管機宜文字。

translations.literal: He was recruited into Gong’s staff as director of confidential documents.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Meng Gong’s staff as director of confidential documents.

sentences.zh: 珙卒，遺表舉賈似道自代，而薦庭芝於似道，庭芝感珙知己，扶其柩葬之興國，即棄官歸，為珙行三年喪。

translations.literal: When Gong died, his final memorial recommended Jia Sidao to replace himself, and recommended Tingzhi to Sidao; Tingzhi, moved by Gong’s knowing him, bore the coffin to burial at Xingguo, then at once left office and returned, observing three years’ mourning for Gong.
translations.idiomatic: At Meng Gong’s death his final memorial named Jia Sidao as successor and commended Tingzhi to him. Grateful for Meng Gong’s trust, Tingzhi bore the coffin to burial at Xingguo, resigned, and observed three years’ mourning for his patron.

sentences.zh: 似道鎮京湖，起為製置司參議，移鎮兩淮，與似道議柵清河五河口，增淮南烽百二十。

translations.literal: Sidao was stationed at Jinghu; Tingzhi was raised as planning staff of the commission, moved to garrison the two Huai, and with Sidao planned palisades at the five river mouths of Qinghe, adding one hundred twenty beacon towers on the Huainan frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When Sidao held Jinghu, Tingzhi became planning staff on his commission, then moved to the two Huai, where together they built palisades at Qinghe’s five river mouths and added a hundred twenty beacon towers along Huainan.

sentences.zh: 繼知濠州，復城荊山以備淮南。

translations.literal: He was next made prefect of Hao, and rebuilt Jingshan city to guard Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made prefect of Hao and rebuilt Jingshan to shield Huainan.

sentences.zh: 皆切中機會。

translations.literal: All cut to the heart of opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Each measure struck at the right moment.

sentences.zh: 開慶元年，似道宣撫京湖，留庭芝權揚州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingqing, Sidao was pacification commissioner of Jinghu and left Tingzhi acting at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingqing year 1, with Sidao pacification commissioner of Jinghu, Tingzhi was left in charge at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋以大兵在蜀，奏知峽州，以防蜀江口。

translations.literal: Soon, because great forces were in Shu, he memorialized to be made prefect of Xia Prefecture to guard the Shu river mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, with major forces in Sichuan, he asked to be made prefect of Xia to guard the Sichuan river mouth.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以趙與芮為淮南製置，李應庚為參議官。

translations.literal: The court made Zhao Yourui Huainan commissioner and Li Yinggeng planning staff.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Zhao Yourui Huainan commissioner and Li Yinggeng as planning staff.

sentences.zh: 應庚發兩路兵城南城，大暑中暍死者數萬。

translations.literal: Yinggeng mobilized troops of both circuits to attack the southern city; in great heat tens of thousands died of sunstroke.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yinggeng marched both circuits’ troops against the southern city; in the midsummer heat tens of thousands died of sunstroke.

sentences.zh: 李亶窺其無謀，奪漣水三城，渡淮奪南城。

translations.literal: Li Dan spied their lack of plan, seized the three cities of Lianshui, crossed the Huai and seized the southern city.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dan, seeing their folly, took the three Lianshui cities, crossed the Huai, and seized the southern city.

sentences.zh: 鄂兵解，庭芝丁母憂去。

translations.literal: When the E troops were relieved, Tingzhi left on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When the relief from Ezhou arrived, Tingzhi left to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 朝議擇守揚者，帝曰：“無如李庭芝。

translations.literal: The court deliberated on choosing a defender of Yang; the emperor said: “None like Li Tingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated who should hold Yangzhou; the emperor said, “No one but Li Tingzhi.

sentences.zh: ”乃奪情主管兩淮製置司事。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon, interrupting mourning, he was put in charge of the two-Huai commission.
translations.idiomatic: ” He was recalled from mourning to head the two-Huai commission.

sentences.zh: 庭芝再破亶兵，殺亶將厲元帥，夷南城而歸。

translations.literal: Tingzhi again defeated Dan’s troops, killed Dan’s general Li Yuanshuai, razed the southern city and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi again routed Li Dan, killed his general Li Yuanshuai, razed the southern city, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年，復敗亶於喬村，破東海、石圃等城。

translations.literal: The next year he again defeated Dan at Qiaocun and broke the cities of Donghai, Shipu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he defeated Dan again at Qiaocun and took Donghai, Shipu, and other cities.

sentences.zh: 又明年，亶降，徙三城民於通、泰之間。

translations.literal: The year after that, Dan surrendered, and the people of the three cities were moved between Tong and Tai.
translations.idiomatic: The year after, Li Dan surrendered and the three cities’ populace was resettled between Tong and Tai.

sentences.zh: 又破蘄縣，殺守將。

translations.literal: He again broke Qizhou and killed the defending general.
translations.idiomatic: He also took Qizhou and killed its defender.

sentences.zh: 庭芝初至揚時，揚新遭火，廬舍盡毀。

translations.literal: When Tingzhi first arrived at Yang, Yang had newly suffered fire and dwellings were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingzhi first reached Yangzhou, the city had just burned and every house lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 州賴鹽為利，而亭戶多亡去，公私蕭然。

translations.literal: The prefecture relied on salt for profit, but the saltern households mostly fled; public and private were alike desolate.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture depended on the salt trade, yet saltern households had fled in droves; public and private coffers alike were empty.

sentences.zh: 庭芝悉貸民負逋，假錢使為屋，屋成又免其假錢，凡一歲，官民居皆具。

translations.literal: Tingzhi fully lent on the people’s overdue arrears, lent money to let them build houses; when houses were completed he again remitted the borrowed money—in all one year, official and private dwellings were all complete.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi canceled overdue debts, lent money for rebuilding, then forgave the loans when houses were finished. Within a year both official quarters and private homes stood restored.

sentences.zh: 鑿河四十里入金沙餘慶場，以省車運。

translations.literal: He cut a canal forty li into the Jinsha Yuqing saltern to save cart transport.
translations.idiomatic: He dug a forty-li canal to the Jinsha Yuqing saltern, sparing cart haulage.

sentences.zh: 兼浚他運河，放亭戶負鹽二百餘萬。

translations.literal: He also dredged other transport canals and released the saltern households’ salt debt of more than two million.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged other transport canals and wrote off more than two million in saltern salt debt.

sentences.zh: 亭民無車運之勞，又得免所負，逃者皆來歸，鹽利大興。

translations.literal: The saltern people had no cart-transport toil, and moreover were freed from what they owed; those who had fled all came back, and salt profits greatly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Saltern workers were spared cart labor and freed of debt; refugees returned, and the salt trade revived.

sentences.zh: 始，平山堂瞰揚城，大元兵至，則構望樓其上，張車弩以射城中。

translations.literal: At first the Pingshan Hall overlooked Yang city; when Great Yuan troops came, they built a watchtower on it and stretched cart-mounted crossbows to shoot into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Pingshan Hall had overlooked the city; when Yuan forces came they built a watchtower there and mounted ballistae to rain bolts on Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 庭芝乃築大城包之，城中募汴南流民二萬人以實之，有詔命為武銳軍。

translations.literal: Tingzhi then built a great wall to wrap it; within the city he recruited twenty thousand refugees from south of Bian to fill it, and an edict named them the Wurui Army.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi encircled it with a great outer wall and enrolled twenty thousand refugees from south of Bian to man it; the court named them the Wurui Army.

sentences.zh: 又大修學，為詩書、俎豆，與士行習射禮。

translations.literal: He also greatly repaired the school, made poetry, books, sacrificial vessels, and with the gentlemen practiced the archery rite.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the school, furnished classics and ritual vessels, and drilled the gentry in archery ceremony.

sentences.zh: 郡中有水旱，即命發廩，不足則以私財振之。

translations.literal: When the commandery had flood or drought, he at once ordered the granaries opened; if insufficient he used private wealth to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: In flood or drought he opened the granaries at once, and when stores ran short he spent his own wealth on relief.

sentences.zh: 揚民德之如父母。

translations.literal: The people of Yang regarded his virtue as toward parents.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yangzhou loved him as a parent.

sentences.zh: 劉槃自淮南入朝，帝問淮事，槃對曰：“李庭芝老成謹重，軍民安之。

translations.literal: Liu Pan entered court from Huainan; the emperor asked about Huai affairs, and Pan replied: “Li Tingzhi is seasoned and careful; military and people are at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pan came to court from Huainan. Asked about the Huai front, he said, “Li Tingzhi is steady and prudent; soldiers and civilians are secure.

sentences.zh: 今邊塵不驚，百度具舉，皆陛下委任得人之效也。”

translations.literal: Now the frontier dust is not alarmed, and the hundred affairs are all raised—this is entirely the effect of Your Majesty’s entrusting men and obtaining the right ones.”
translations.idiomatic: The border is quiet and every undertaking prospers—all because Your Majesty appoints the right men.”

sentences.zh: 鹹淳五年，北兵圍襄陽急，夏貴入援，大敗虎尾州；

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianchun, northern troops urgently besieged Xiangyang; Xia Gui entered to relieve and was greatly defeated at Huwei;
translations.idiomatic: In Xianchun year 5 the northern army pressed Xiangyang hard. Xia Gui marched to relieve it and was routed at Huwei;

sentences.zh: 範文虎總諸兵再入，又敗，文虎以輕舠遁，兵亂，士卒溺漢水死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Fan Wenhu commanded all troops to enter again and was again defeated; Wenhu fled in a light boat, the army fell into disorder, and very many soldiers drowned in the Han River.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wenhu led a second relief force and was beaten again; he fled in a light craft while troops broke ranks, and countless men drowned in the Han.

sentences.zh: 冬，命庭芝以京湖製置大使督師援襄陽。

translations.literal: In winter, Tingzhi was ordered as Grand Commissioner of the Jinghu Commission to supervise troops relieving Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Tingzhi was ordered as Jinghu Grand Commissioner to lead the Xiangyang relief.

sentences.zh: 文虎聞庭芝至，貽書似道曰：“吾將兵數萬入襄陽，一戰可平，但無使聽命於京閫，事成則功歸恩相矣。

translations.literal: When Wenhu heard Tingzhi had come, he sent a letter to Sidao saying: “I will lead several tens of thousands of troops into Xiangyang; one battle can settle it—only do not let them take orders from the capital military commission; when the affair is done the merit will return to the Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Tingzhi’s arrival, Wenhu wrote Sidao: “I have tens of thousands of men; one battle will end it—only keep me from orders out of the capital command. Then the credit will be yours.

sentences.zh: ”似道喜，即除文虎福州觀察使，其兵從中製之。

translations.literal: ” Sidao was pleased and at once appointed Wenhu observation commissioner of Fuzhou, and his troops were controlled from the center.
translations.idiomatic: ” Sidao was delighted, made Wenhu observation commissioner of Fuzhou, and kept his army under central control.

sentences.zh: 文虎日攜美妾，走馬擊球軍中為樂。

translations.literal: Wenhu daily carried beautiful concubines and in the army amused himself with horse-riding and ball games.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhu spent his days with concubines, riding and playing ball in camp.

sentences.zh: 庭芝屢欲進兵，曰：“吾取旨未至也。

translations.literal: Tingzhi repeatedly wished to advance the army, but said: “I have not yet received the imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi repeatedly urged an advance, saying, “I have not yet received the imperial order.

sentences.zh: ”明年六月，漢水溢，文虎不得已始一出師，未至鹿門，中道遁去。

translations.literal: ” In the sixth month of the next year the Han overflowed; Wenhu, having no choice, at last set out once; before reaching Lumen he fled midway.
translations.idiomatic: ” The next sixth month the Han flooded; Wenhu at last marched once, then fled before reaching Lumen.

sentences.zh: 庭芝數自劾請代，不允，竟失襄陽。

translations.literal: Tingzhi several times memorialized self-impeachment and begged to be replaced; it was not permitted, and in the end Xiangyang was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi repeatedly asked to be relieved; the court refused, and Xiangyang fell.

sentences.zh: 陳宜中請誅文虎，似道庇之，止降一官知安慶府，而貶庭芝及部將蘇劉義、範友信廣南。

translations.literal: Chen Yizhong asked to execute Wenhu; Sidao sheltered him, only demoting him one rank to prefect of Anqing, while Tingzhi and his subordinate generals Su Liuyi and Fan Youxin were banished to Guangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yizhong demanded Wenhu’s execution; Sidao shielded him with a single-rank demotion to Anqing prefect, while Tingzhi and generals Su Liuyi and Fan Youxin were exiled to Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 庭芝罷居京口。

translations.literal: Tingzhi left office and dwelt at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi retired to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，大元兵圍揚州，製置印應雷暴死，即起庭芝製置兩淮。

translations.literal: Before long, Great Yuan troops besieged Yangzhou; Commission Superintendent Yin Yinglei died suddenly, and Tingzhi was at once raised as commissioner of the two Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuan forces besieged Yangzhou; commissioner Yin Yinglei died suddenly, and Tingzhi was recalled to command the two Huai.

sentences.zh: 庭芝請分淮西夏貴，而己得專力淮東，從之。

translations.literal: Tingzhi asked to divide the Huai—Xia Gui on the west, while he himself could concentrate on the Huai east—and it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi asked to split the front: Xia Gui would hold western Huai while he focused on the east, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 十年，築清河口，詔以為清河軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he built the Qinghe mouth, and an edict made it Qinghe Army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he fortified the Qinghe mouth, which the court chartered as Qinghe Army.

sentences.zh: 十二月，大元兵破鄂，詔天下勤王，庭芝首遣兵為諸道倡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Great Yuan troops broke E, and an edict called the realm to arms; Tingzhi was first to dispatch troops as leader for all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Yuan forces took Ezhou; the court called for loyalist armies, and Tingzhi was first to send troops, leading every circuit.

sentences.zh: 德祐元年春，似道兵潰蕪湖，沿江諸郡或降或遁，無一人能守者。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Deyou, Sidao’s troops were routed at Wuhu; along the river every prefecture either surrendered or fled—none could defend.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Deyou year 1, Sidao’s army was shattered at Wuhu; along the Yangtze prefectures surrendered or fled—none held.

sentences.zh: 庭芝率所部郡縣城守。

translations.literal: Tingzhi led his districts and counties in defending the cities.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi held every city in his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 有李虎者持招降榜入揚州，庭芝誅虎，焚其榜。

translations.literal: There was one Li Hu who carried a surrender proclamation into Yangzhou; Tingzhi executed Hu and burned the proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Li Hu brought a surrender placard into Yangzhou; Tingzhi killed him and burned it.

sentences.zh: 總製張俊出戰，持孟之縉書來招降，庭芝焚書，梟俊五人於市。

translations.literal: General-in-chief Zhang Jun went out to fight, bearing Meng Zhijin’s letter to summon surrender; Tingzhi burned the letter and exposed Jun and five others in the market.
translations.idiomatic: General Zhang Jun came out to fight bearing Meng Zhijin’s surrender letter; Tingzhi burned it and displayed Jun and five others in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 而日調苗再成戰其南，許文德戰其北，薑才、施忠戰其中。

translations.literal: Daily he deployed Miao Zaicheng to fight on the south, Xu Wende on the north, Jiang Cai and Shi Zhong in the center.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he sent Miao Zaicheng to the south, Xu Wende to the north, and Jiang Cai and Shi Zhong in the center.

sentences.zh: 時出金帛牛酒燕犒將士，人人為之死鬥。

translations.literal: He often brought out gold, silk, cattle, and wine to feast and reward the officers and soldiers; every man fought to the death for him.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted his troops on gold, silk, cattle, and wine, and every man fought for him unto death.

sentences.zh: 朝廷亦以督府金勞之，加庭芝參知政事。

translations.literal: The court also used gold from the command headquarters to reward him, and advanced Tingzhi to Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent command gold as reward and promoted Tingzhi to Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 七月，以知樞密院事征入朝，徙夏貴知揚州，貴不至，事遂已。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was summoned to court as Director of the Privy Council; Xia Gui was moved to know Yangzhou, but Gui did not arrive, and the affair ended.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was summoned as Director of the Privy Council; Xia Gui was named to replace him at Yangzhou but never came, and the plan lapsed.

sentences.zh: 十月，大元丞相伯顏入臨安，留元帥阿術軍鎮江以遏淮兵。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Great Yuan Chancellor Bayan entered Lin’an; he left Marshal Achu’s army to garrison Zhenjiang and contain Huai troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Chancellor Bayan entered Lin’an and left Marshal Achu at Zhenjiang to pin the Huai armies.

sentences.zh: 阿術攻揚久不拔，乃築長圍困之。

translations.literal: Achu attacked Yang for a long time without taking it, and then built a long encirclement to besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: Achu assaulted Yangzhou for months without success, then threw up a long encirclement.

sentences.zh: 冬，城中食盡，死者滿道。

translations.literal: In winter, food in the city was exhausted; the dead filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: By winter the city was starving; corpses choked the streets.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，饑益甚，赴濠水死者日數百，道有死者，眾爭割啖之立盡。

translations.literal: In the second month of the next year famine grew worse; daily hundreds threw themselves into the moat water and died; where there were dead on the road, the crowd strove to cut and eat them on the spot until nothing remained.
translations.idiomatic: The next second month famine worsened; hundreds leapt into the moat each day. Where a body lay in the street, crowds fought to carve and devour it on the spot.

sentences.zh: 宋亡，謝太后及瀛國公為詔諭之降，庭芝登城曰：“奉詔守城，未聞有詔諭降也。

translations.literal: When Song perished, Empress Dowager Xie and the Duke of Ying State issued an edict instructing surrender; Tingzhi ascended the wall and said: “I received an edict to hold the city; I have not heard of an edict instructing surrender.
translations.idiomatic: After Song fell, Empress Dowager Xie and Emperor Yingguo sent orders to surrender. Tingzhi mounted the wall and said, “I was ordered to defend this city; I have heard no order to surrender.

sentences.zh: ”已而兩宮入朝，至瓜州，復詔庭芝曰：“比詔卿納款，日久未報，豈未悉吾意，尚欲固圉邪？

translations.literal: ” Before long the two palaces entered court; arriving at Guazhou, they again edicted Tingzhi: “The recent edict told you to submit; days pass without reply—do you perhaps not yet understand Our intent, and still wish to hold the walls firm?
translations.idiomatic: ” Soon the imperial household went north; at Guazhou they wrote again: “We ordered you to submit, yet days pass without answer—do you still not grasp Our meaning, and mean to hold the walls?”

sentences.zh: 今吾與嗣君既已臣伏，卿尚為誰守之？

translations.literal: Now that I and the heir have already submitted as subjects, for whom are you still holding the city?
translations.idiomatic: Now that the heir and I have already submitted, for whom are you still holding out?

sentences.zh: ”庭芝不答，命發弩射使者，斃一人，餘皆退去。

translations.literal: ” Tingzhi did not answer, ordered crossbows loosed at the envoys, killed one man, and the rest all withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi made no reply, ordered crossbows fired at the envoys, killed one, and the rest withdrew.

sentences.zh: 薑才出兵奪兩宮，不克，復閉城守。

translations.literal: Jiang Cai led troops out to seize the two palaces, failed, and again closed the city to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Cai led troops out to recover the two palaces, failed, and the city was shut again for defense.

sentences.zh: 三月，夏貴以淮西降，阿術驅降兵至城下以示之，旌旗蔽野，幕客有以言覘庭芝者，庭芝曰：“吾惟一死而已。

translations.literal: In the third month Xia Gui surrendered with Huai West; Achu drove surrendered troops to the foot of the wall to display them, banners blotting the fields. A staff member tried to sound Tingzhi out; Tingzhi said: “I have only death left.”
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Xia Gui surrendered Huai West; Achu marched surrendered troops to the walls as a display, banners covering the plain. When a staff member tried to probe him, Tingzhi said, “I have only death left.”

sentences.zh: ”阿術使者持詔來招降，庭芝開壁納使者，斬之，焚詔陴上。

translations.literal: ” Achu’s envoy came bearing an edict to summon surrender; Tingzhi opened the rampart and admitted the envoy, beheaded him, and burned the edict on the parapet.
translations.idiomatic: Achu’s envoy came with an edict offering surrender; Tingzhi opened the gate, admitted him, beheaded him, and burned the edict on the wall.

sentences.zh: 已而知淮安州許文德、知盱眙軍張思聰、知泗州劉興祖皆以糧盡降。

translations.literal: Soon it was learned that Xu Wende, prefect of Huai’an, Zhang Sicong, military commissioner of Xuyi, and Liu Xingzu, prefect of Sizhou, had all surrendered when grain was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that Xu Wende of Huai’an, Zhang Sicong of Xuyi, and Liu Xingzu of Sizhou had all surrendered when their grain ran out.

sentences.zh: 庭芝猶括民間粟以給兵，粟盡，令官人出粟，粟又盡，令將校出粟，雜牛皮、曲糵以給之。

translations.literal: Tingzhi still levied grain from the populace to supply the troops; when grain was gone he ordered officials to contribute grain; when that too was gone he ordered officers to contribute, mixing ox hide and ferment to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi still requisitioned civilian grain for the army; when it was gone he ordered officials to give grain, then officers, mixing ox hide and ferment mash to feed the men.

sentences.zh: 兵有烹子而食者，猶日出苦戰。

translations.literal: Some soldiers boiled their sons to eat, yet still went out to fight bitterly each day.
translations.idiomatic: Some soldiers boiled their children for food, yet still went out to fight bitterly every day.

sentences.zh: 七月，阿術請赦庭芝焚詔之罪，使之降，有詔從之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Achu requested pardon for Tingzhi’s crime of burning the edict so that he might surrender; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Achu asked that Tingzhi be pardoned for burning the edict so he might surrender; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 庭芝亦不納。

translations.literal: Tingzhi still would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi still refused.

sentences.zh: 是月，益王遣使以少保、左丞相召庭芝，庭芝以朱煥守揚，與薑才將兵七千人東入海，至泰州，阿術將兵追圍之。

translations.literal: That month Prince Yi sent envoys to summon Tingzhi as Junior Guardian and left grand councilor; Tingzhi left Zhu Huan to defend Yang, and with Jiang Cai led seven thousand troops eastward into the sea, reaching Taizhou, where Achu pursued and besieged them.
translations.idiomatic: That month Prince Yi summoned Tingzhi as Junior Guardian and left grand councilor; Tingzhi left Zhu Huan to hold Yangzhou and with Jiang Cai led seven thousand men east toward the sea to Taizhou, where Achu pursued and besieged them.

sentences.zh: 朱煥既以城降，驅庭芝將士妻子至泰州城下，陴將孫貴、胡惟孝等開門降。

translations.literal: Zhu Huan having surrendered the city, he drove the wives and children of Tingzhi’s officers and soldiers to the foot of Taizhou’s wall; defenders Sun Gui, Hu Weixiao, and others opened the gate and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Huan surrendered the city, he drove the families of Tingzhi’s men to Taizhou’s walls; defenders Sun Gui and Hu Weixiao opened the gates and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 庭芝聞變，赴蓮池，水淺不得死。

translations.literal: Hearing of the change, Tingzhi went to Lotus Pond; the water was shallow and he could not die.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard what had happened, Tingzhi threw himself into Lotus Pond, but the water was too shallow and he could not drown.

sentences.zh: 被執至揚州，朱煥請曰：“揚自用兵以來，積骸滿野，皆庭芝與才所為，不殺之何俟？

translations.literal: Seized and taken to Yangzhou, Zhu Huan requested: “Since war began at Yang, corpses have piled across the fields—all the work of Tingzhi and Cai. If we do not kill them, what are we waiting for?”
translations.idiomatic: Captured and taken to Yangzhou, Zhu Huan said, “Since the fighting began at Yangzhou, the fields have been heaped with corpses—all Tingzhi and Cai’s doing. Why wait to kill them?”

sentences.zh: ”於是斬之。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon they were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: They were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 死之日，揚之民皆泣下。

translations.literal: On the day of their deaths, the people of Yang all wept.
translations.idiomatic: On the day they died, the people of Yangzhou wept.

sentences.zh: 有宋應龍者為泰州谘議官，泰守孫良臣之弟舜臣自軍中來說降，良臣召應龍與計，應龍極陳國家恩澤，君臣大義，請殺舜臣以戒持二心者，良臣不得已殺之。

translations.literal: There was a Song Yinglong who served as Taizhou deliberation officer; the prefect Sun Liangchen’s younger brother Shunchen came from the army to urge surrender. Liangchen summoned Yinglong to consult; Yinglong set forth at length the state’s grace and the great righteousness between ruler and minister, and asked that Shunchen be killed to warn those of divided loyalty; Liangchen had no choice but to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yinglong was Taizhou deliberation officer; Prefect Sun Liangchen’s brother Shunchen came from the army to urge surrender. Liangchen consulted Yinglong, who spoke at length of the state’s grace and loyalty between ruler and minister and asked that Shunchen be killed to warn waverers; Liangchen reluctantly killed him.

sentences.zh: 及泰州降，應龍夫婦自經死。

translations.literal: When Taizhou surrendered, Yinglong and his wife hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizhou fell, Yinglong and his wife hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 提刑司諮議褚一正置司高郵，督戰被創，沒水死。

translations.literal: Judicial intendant deliberation officer Chu Yizheng was posted at Gaoyou, urged the fight, was wounded, and died drowning.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yizheng, deliberation officer of the judicial intendant’s office, was posted at Gaoyou, urged the fighting, was wounded, and drowned.

sentences.zh: 知興化縣胡拱辰，城破亦死。

translations.literal: Hu Gongchen, magistrate of Xinghua County, also died when the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Gongchen, magistrate of Xinghua, also died when his city fell.

sentences.zh: 論曰：楊棟學本伊、洛，而尼於權臣，速謗召尤，誰之過歟？

translations.literal: The judgment says: Yang Dong’s learning was rooted in the Yi and Luo schools, yet he was constrained by a powerful minister; swiftly slandered and inviting blame—whose fault was it?
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Yang Dong’s learning came from the Yi and Luo traditions, yet he was hemmed in by a powerful minister, quickly slandered and blamed—whose fault was that?

sentences.zh: 姚希得藹然君子。

translations.literal: Yao Xide was a gentle and amiable gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xide was a gentle, amiable gentleman.

sentences.zh: 包恢以嚴為治，抑以衰世之民非可以縱馳待之耶？

translations.literal: Bao Hui governed by severity—is it not because the people of a declining age cannot be treated with lax indulgence?
translations.idiomatic: Bao Hui governed with severity—was that not because a people in a declining age cannot be handled with lax indulgence?

sentences.zh: 常挺、陳宗禮咸通濟，著聲望。

translations.literal: Chang Ting and Chen Zongli were both versed in statecraft and won renown.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Ting and Chen Zongli were both skilled in statecraft and won wide renown.

sentences.zh: 常楙晚訟皇子竑事，光明正大，公義炳然。

translations.literal: Chang Mao in his later years pleaded the case of Prince Qi—open and upright, public justice shining clear.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Mao in his later years pleaded the case of Prince Qi—open, upright, and radiant with public justice.

sentences.zh: 家鉉翁義不二君，足為臣軌。

translations.literal: Jia Xuanweng’s loyalty admitted no second ruler—enough to be a model for ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xuanweng’s loyalty to one ruler alone is enough to stand as a model for ministers.

sentences.zh: 李庭芝死於國難，其可憫哉！

translations.literal: Li Tingzhi died in the nation’s calamity—how pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: Li Tingzhi died in the nation’s calamity—how pitiable!
